article.title: Zemi #1: Innovations in Mobile Web Technologies for Efficient Visual Information Processing
article.subtitle: This event explores efficient mobile technologies for image processing and concept map reconstruction.

content.text: On Friday, October 2, 2026, the Media, Game and Mobile (MGM) Laboratory held its very first Zemi session.

Zemi is a weekly session organized by the MGM Laboratory where master's students can share and discuss their ongoing research. It gives them a chance to present what they have been working on, get feedback, and have a discussion with lecturers and other members of the laboratory.
For the first session, we had two master's students presenting their research, along with lecturers and other members of the MGM Laboratory joining the discussion.
The First Zemi Session
The first Zemi was held in a hybrid format at Teater Heuristik, Building A, 2nd Floor, from 13.00 to 15.00 WIB. We were joined by Ir. Aryo Pinandito, S.T.,
M.MT
., Ph.D. and Eriq Muhammad Adams Jonemaro, S.T., M.Kom. as lecturers who also took part in the discussion and shared their perspectives on the presented research.
For this first session, we had two presenters.
The first was Muhamad Zidane Arfani, who presented his research entitled:
“Quality and Performance Analysis of Lanczos Resampling Image with Hamming Filter in ReactJS Mobile Web Application”

His research looks at image resampling using the Lanczos method combined with a Hamming filter, specifically in a ReactJS-based mobile web application. The research focuses on looking at both the quality of the resulting images and the performance of the approach.
The second presenter was Syahrizal Azzuri, who presented:
“Efisiensi Rekonstruksi Kit-Build Concept Map Pada Platform Inklusif Berbasis Smartphone”

His research focuses on the efficiency of reconstructing Kit-Build Concept Maps through an inclusive smartphone-based platform. It explores how smartphone technology can be used to support more accessible learning and knowledge representation.
Two different topics, but that's also what makes sessions like this interesting.
More Than Just a Presentation

Although the main part of Zemi is the research presentation, it is not really meant to be just a presentation session. After each presentation, there is a discussion where presenters can get questions, suggestions, and different perspectives about their research. Sometimes a question from someone else can make you look at your own research differently. And I think that's one of the most useful parts of having a regular research-sharing session. For the other members of the laboratory, it is also a chance to see what everyone else is working on. MGM itself has research that covers different areas, including media, games, mobile applications, and interactive technology. So even when a topic isn't directly related to what you're working on, there is usually still something interesting to take away from it.
Starting Something New

The first Zemi session is basically the start of what we hope will become a regular part of life in the MGM Laboratory. By doing it every week, researchers have a place to regularly share their progress, talk about problems they are facing, and get feedback from other people in the laboratory. More importantly, it gives research a space to be discussed instead of being something that happens quietly on its own. Of course, the first session isn't going to be perfect. There will always be things that we can improve as we go.

The important thing is that we started. Our first Zemi brought together two research topics, two presenters, lecturers, and members of the laboratory for an afternoon of discussion and learning. And hopefully, this is just the first of many.
See you at the next Zemi.
More Info on:
https://zemi.ac/events/1

article.title: A Shopping Technology Review Links Lab MGM and ITS Surabaya
article.subtitle: An ITS researcher coauthored a 2021 literature review on shopping technology together with Universitas Brawijaya and Bina Nusantara University researchers.

content.text: A 2021 review of shopping technologies brought together researchers from three Indonesian universities, including one from Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember in Surabaya, on the north coast of East Java, commonly known as ITS.

ITS is a public institute focused on engineering and technology, one of the older technical universities in Indonesia. The paper, A Literature Review: Feasibility Study of Technology to Improve Shopping Experience, was published in the journal Procedia Computer Science in 2021 as part of a computer science conference proceedings. Rather than running a new experiment, it works as a synthesis of prior studies, weighing three approaches side by side: smart shopping trolleys that track items as shoppers walk the aisles, virtual reality shopping experiences that let a customer browse a store remotely, and cashier-less checkout systems that let customers leave a store without stopping at a register. The authors frame each option around whether it is realistic to deploy today, not just whether it works in a lab.
Who wrote it

Muhammad Attamimi, affiliated with ITS, coauthored the paper with Herman Tolle of Universitas Brawijaya, along with Heraldo Y. Purwantono and Alexander A.S. Gunawan of the Computer Science Department at Bina Nusantara University, and one further coauthor. The paper is listed among Lab MGM's publications through Tolle's involvement, and its title identifies it as a literature review rather than a new experiment.

props.caption: Image: Arifhidayat, CC BY-SA 3.0. The main library building of Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember in Surabaya, East Java.

content.text: As with most of the connections behind Lab MGM's Trusted By logos, this one is a research coauthorship rather than a signed agreement between ITS and Universitas Brawijaya. It shows two Indonesian computer science departments working through the same literature review, alongside a private university in Jakarta, rather than a formal institutional tie between the two public campuses. It is a modest connection by design: one paper, one shared author list, and no ongoing program tying the institutions together beyond that.
Source: https://scholar.its.ac.id/en/publications/a-literature-review-feasibility-study-of-technology-to-improve-sh/ and https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1877050921000351

article.title: A Guest Lecture Ties Lab MGM to Ritsumeikan University
article.subtitle: A Ritsumeikan doctoral student and FILKOM alumnus gave a guest lecture in 2022, and separately coauthored a paper with Universitas Brawijaya researchers.

content.text: In July 2022, a graduate of the Faculty of Computer Science, Universitas Brawijaya, returned to speak to his old campus, though by then he was studying on the other side of the world.

Mury Fajar Dewantoro finished his degree at FILKOM UB in 2010 and went on to pursue a doctorate at Ritsumeikan University in Japan. On 5 July 2022, FILKOM invited him back as the speaker for the fourth session of its Interaction Design webinar series, a recurring lineup of sessions on interface and interaction topics aimed at students. Dewantoro walked the audience through how games give non-player characters believable, responsive behavior, and how that behavior shapes the way a player experiences the game. His listed research interests at Ritsumeikan include procedural content generation, the practice of having software produce game content automatically rather than by hand. The session was a single guest lecture arranged by the faculty, not a cooperation agreement between the two universities.
A second, separate connection

Dewantoro also turns up as a coauthor on a paper unrelated to that lecture. Titled TOPSIS for Mobile Based Group and Personal Decision Support System, it was published in the journal Register: Jurnal Ilmiah Teknologi Sistem Informasi in February 2021. TOPSIS, short for Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution, is a ranking method the paper uses to build personal and group travel recommendations for tourists visiting Malang. His coauthors, Ratih Kartika Dewi, Eriq Muhammad Adams Jonemaro, Agi Putra Kharisma, and Najla Alia Farah, are Universitas Brawijaya researchers, and the paper is listed among Lab MGM's publications.

props.caption: Image: J o, CC BY-SA 3.0. Ritsumeikan University's Biwako-Kusatsu Campus in Shiga, Japan, one of the university's graduate research campuses.

content.text: Put together, the two threads describe the same kind of link: individual researchers crossing paths through study abroad, a shared paper, and one invited talk, rather than any formal arrangement between Ritsumeikan University and Universitas Brawijaya. FILKOM UB keeps this kind of connection alive by inviting its own graduates to share what they are learning once they move on to universities elsewhere, and Dewantoro's 2022 session is one small example of that practice.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/07/05/mengetahui-dasar-ai-dan-interaksi-pengguna-dalam-game/

article.title: Concept Maps and Augmented Reality Link Lab MGM and POLINEMA
article.subtitle: Researchers at Politeknik Negeri Malang have repeatedly coauthored studies with Universitas Brawijaya and Japanese collaborators, a pattern of research coauthorship rather than a formal agreement.

content.text: Down the road from Universitas Brawijaya, researchers at Politeknik Negeri Malang, commonly called POLINEMA, keep turning up as coauthors on the same kind of papers Lab MGM produces.

POLINEMA is a state polytechnic focused on applied engineering education, separate from Universitas Brawijaya but based in the same city. In 2024, the journal Research and Practice in Technology Enhanced Learning published Evaluating the Kit-Build Concept Mapping Process Using Sub-Map Scoring. Its authors are Ridwan Rismanto, Yusuke Hayashi, and Tsukasa Hirashima of Hiroshima University in Japan, Aryo Pinandito of Universitas Brawijaya, and Banni Satria Andoko of POLINEMA. The paper examines Kit-Build, a method where students build concept maps from a kit of prepared elements rather than free drawing, and proposes scoring smaller sub-maps of a larger concept map to evaluate the building process more closely.
A second paper, a year later

POLINEMA researchers Mustika Mentari, Yan Watequlis Syaifudin, and Alfiandi Aulia Rahmadani also appear on A Proposal of In Situ Authoring Tool with Visual-Inertial Sensor Fusion for Outdoor Location-Based Augmented Reality, published in the journal Electronics in January 2025 alongside Okayama University and Universitas Brawijaya researchers. Mentari holds a joint appointment at both Okayama University and POLINEMA. That paper describes a tool for placing virtual objects at real outdoor locations directly from a smartphone, aimed at simplifying augmented reality content creation for developers working in the field rather than at a desk.

props.caption: Image: Supra Syitno, CC BY-SA 3.0. A street in Malang, East Java, the city that is home to both Universitas Brawijaya and Politeknik Negeri Malang.

content.text: Neither publication reflects a signed cooperation agreement between POLINEMA and Universitas Brawijaya or Lab MGM specifically. What the record shows is a recurring pattern: POLINEMA staff, largely from its Department of Information Technology, keep contributing to the same lines of research as Lab MGM affiliated researchers, through two separate Japanese connections. Andoko's concept mapping paper runs through Hiroshima University, while Mentari, Syaifudin, and Rahmadani's augmented reality paper runs through Okayama University instead.
Source: https://rptel.apsce.net/index.php/RPTEL/article/view/2024-19021 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373937832_Evaluating_the_kit-build_concept_mapping_process_using_sub-map_scoring

article.title: Two Augmented Reality Papers Connect Lab MGM and Okayama University
article.subtitle: Researchers from Okayama University and Universitas Brawijaya have coauthored a recurring line of outdoor augmented reality studies, not a signed institutional agreement.

content.text: Two recent papers on outdoor augmented reality carry both an Okayama University and a Universitas Brawijaya address for the same author, and that overlap is where this connection comes from.

Komang Candra Brata is listed with a dual affiliation, the Department of Information and Communication Systems at Okayama University in Japan and the Department of Informatics Engineering at Universitas Brawijaya, on both papers. His frequent coauthor is Nobuo Funabiki of Okayama University, together with fellow Okayama researcher Yohanes Yohanie Fridelin Panduman. Both papers focus on outdoor location-based augmented reality, the practice of anchoring digital content to specific real-world coordinates so it appears in the right place when viewed through a phone or headset.
Two papers, two years

The first, An Enhancement of Outdoor Location-Based Augmented Reality Anchor Precision through VSLAM and Google Street View, appeared in the journal Sensors on 9 February 2024, with Evianita Dewi Fajrianti of Okayama University as a fourth coauthor. VSLAM, short for visual simultaneous localization and mapping, is combined here with Google Street View imagery to line up virtual objects more precisely with real outdoor locations than a phone's GPS and compass alone can manage. The second paper, A Proposal of In Situ Authoring Tool with Visual-Inertial Sensor Fusion for Outdoor Location-Based Augmented Reality, was published in the journal Electronics on 17 January 2025, adding coauthors from Politeknik Negeri Malang to the same research line and describing a tool that lets a developer place virtual content on site using only a smartphone, without writing custom code for each location.

props.caption: Image: Setouchi, CC BY-SA 3.0. The Tsushima Campus of Okayama University, home to the Graduate School of Natural Science and Technology.
Image: C.Suthorn, CC BY-SA 4.0. A generic augmented reality headset, shown for illustration only and not the device used in the research described here.

content.text: Neither paper points to a cooperation agreement between Okayama University and Universitas Brawijaya. What they show is a working relationship between individual researchers who keep publishing together, with Brata's joint appointment acting as the bridge between the two institutions and Lab MGM's ongoing interest in augmented reality research.
Source: https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/2/342 and https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/24/4/1161

article.title: An IoT Platform Paper Links Lab MGM and INSTIKI in Bali
article.subtitle: Researchers from INSTIKI in Denpasar coauthored a 2025 study on the SEMAR internet-of-things server platform together with Okayama University and Universitas Brawijaya researchers.

content.text: Bali is a long way from Malang, but a shared research platform brought researchers from Institut Bisnis dan Teknologi Indonesia, known as INSTIKI, into the same paper as Lab MGM's Komang Candra Brata.

INSTIKI is a private institute in Denpasar focused on business and technology education. The paper connecting it to Lab MGM, published in the journal Information on 5 February 2025, describes a way to automate the setup of sensor inputs for SEMAR, an application server platform for connecting internet-connected devices such as smart lights, water heaters, and room temperature monitors. Its authors span two institutions: Nobuo Funabiki, Yohanes Yohanie Fridelin Panduman, and Komang Candra Brata of Okayama University's Graduate School of Natural Science and Technology, and I Nyoman Darma Kotama, Anak Agung Surya Pradhana, and I Gusti Made Ngurah Desnanjaya, who are affiliated with INSTIKI's Department of Computer System Engineering in Denpasar.
A research link, not an agreement

Kotama and Pradhana hold joint appointments at both Okayama University and INSTIKI, which is the likely route through which this group came together. Brata, who is also affiliated with Universitas Brawijaya's Department of Informatics Engineering in his other published work, is the connection that puts this paper among Lab MGM's listed publications. The paper reports testing the approach on three practical setups: a smart light, a water heater, and a room temperature monitor. There is no indication of a signed cooperation agreement between INSTIKI and Universitas Brawijaya. What exists is one shared paper, built by researchers who already work together at Okayama, with INSTIKI's involvement running through two of its own faculty.

props.caption: Image: trezy humanoiz, CC BY 2.0. An aerial view of the Bajra Sandhi Monument in Denpasar, Bali, the city where INSTIKI is based.

content.text: For a lab whose research reaches from Malang to Okayama, a coauthor in Denpasar is a small but real extension of the same network, worth describing plainly for what it is: a paper written together, not an institutional tie between the two campuses.
Source: https://www.mdpi.com/2078-2489/16/2/108 and https://doi.org/10.3390/info16020108

article.title: Mengenal Pengembangan Aplikasi Perangkat Bergerak
article.subtitle: Sebuah buku ajar membahas perangkat bergerak dari konsep dasar sampai praktik membangun aplikasinya.

content.text: Ponsel sudah menjadi bagian dari kehidupan sehari-hari. Namun membangun aplikasi yang berjalan di dalamnya menuntut pemahaman yang lebih luas daripada sekadar menulis kode. Buku ini disusun untuk menutup jarak itu, dari pengenalan perangkat sampai praktik pengembangan.

props.caption: Ponsel Android generasi awal. Gambar: Syced, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Buku ini diterbitkan pada 2017 oleh UB Press dan ditulis oleh empat peneliti di bidang teknologi informasi. Sasaran pembacanya jelas: mahasiswa, dosen, dan praktisi yang ingin memulai atau merapikan cara kerja mereka dalam membangun aplikasi bergerak.
Dua bagian, satu alur

Isi buku dibagi menjadi dua bagian besar. Bagian pertama membahas konsep, bagian kedua membahas implementasi. Urutan ini disengaja, karena pembaca diajak memahami lebih dulu mengapa sebuah pendekatan dipilih sebelum mencobanya.
Konsep: perkembangan teknologi bergerak, karakteristik aplikasi, perangkat keras, dan konsep pengembangan.
Implementasi: lingkungan kerja pengembangan dan tiga pendekatan membangun aplikasi.
Setiap bagian dilengkapi latihan untuk menguji pemahaman.

props.caption: Aplikasi bergerak kini menangani banyak pekerjaan harian. Gambar: Acabashi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Bagian konsep tidak langsung membahas kode. Pembaca diajak melihat bagaimana perangkat bergerak tumbuh, sistem operasi apa saja yang bersaing, dan bagaimana bentuk perangkat memengaruhi pengalaman pengguna. Konteks ini sering dilewati pemula, padahal keputusan teknis sehari-hari bertumpu padanya.
Bagian implementasi lebih membumi. Di sini pembaca mengenal alat pengembangan, menyiapkan lingkungan kerja, lalu membandingkan pendekatan yang tersedia beserta konsekuensinya.

Buku ini juga memuat keterangan tentang aturan hak cipta dan sanksi pelanggarannya. Detail kecil seperti ini jarang muncul di buku sejenis, dan berguna bagi mahasiswa yang karyanya akan dinilai secara akademik.

Posisi buku ini adalah rujukan awal, bukan panduan lengkap untuk satu teknologi tertentu. Untuk pembaca yang baru masuk ke pengembangan aplikasi bergerak, urutan konsep lalu praktik seperti ini masuk akal, karena setiap keputusan teknis punya alasan yang bisa dipelajari lebih dulu.
Sumber: Tolle et al. (2017). Pengembangan Aplikasi Perangkat Bergerak. UB Press.

article.title: Tiga Pendekatan Membangun Aplikasi Mobile
article.subtitle: Native, mobile web, atau hybrid. Setiap pilihan membawa konsekuensi pada biaya, kecepatan, dan jangkauan perangkat.

content.text: Saat akan membangun aplikasi bergerak, pertanyaan pertama biasanya bukan bahasa pemrograman apa yang dipakai, melainkan pendekatan apa yang akan dipilih. Buku ini membahas tiga pilihan yang tersedia dan menempatkannya dalam satu perbandingan yang jelas.

props.caption: Lingkungan pengembangan untuk aplikasi native. Gambar: Google LLC, CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Pendekatan native

Pendekatan native berarti aplikasi dibangun khusus untuk satu platform, memakai bahasa dan perkakas resmi platform tersebut. Hasilnya biasanya paling mulus, karena aplikasi bisa memakai seluruh kemampuan perangkat. Harganya adalah biaya pengembangan, sebab tiap platform perlu dikerjakan sendiri.
Pendekatan mobile web

Pendekatan mobile web membangun aplikasi dengan teknologi web dan menjalankannya di peramban ponsel. Satu kode bisa dipakai di banyak perangkat, dan pembaruan tidak perlu melewati toko aplikasi. Batasnya ada pada akses ke fitur perangkat dan pada pengalaman yang terasa kurang menyatu.
Pendekatan hybrid

Pendekatan hybrid mengambil jalan tengah. Aplikasi ditulis dengan teknologi web, lalu dibungkus agar bisa dipasang seperti aplikasi biasa. Tim tetap mendapat satu basis kode, sementara pengguna mendapat ikon di layar utama.

Perbedaan ketiganya terasa paling jelas saat proyek tumbuh. Fitur yang menuntut kinerja tinggi, seperti pengolahan gambar atau pembacaan sensor, lebih nyaman dikerjakan secara native. Fitur yang isinya sering berubah, seperti katalog atau formulir, lebih murah dirawat lewat web.

props.caption: Perangkat bergerak generasi awal. Gambar: Syced, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Yang menarik dari pembahasan ini bukan daftar kelebihan tiap pendekatan, melainkan cara memilihnya. Tidak ada satu jawaban yang benar untuk semua proyek. Jumlah platform yang harus dilayani, anggaran, dan kebutuhan akses ke perangkat keras adalah pertanyaan yang menentukan.
Buku ini juga menekankan bahwa pemahaman konsep tetap dibutuhkan sebelum memilih alat. Tanpa itu, perbandingan pendekatan hanya menjadi daftar istilah.
Sumber: Tolle et al. (2017). Pengembangan Aplikasi Perangkat Bergerak. UB Press.

article.title: Inside a HomeCare App Study at Rumah Sakit Semen Gresik
article.subtitle: A 2021 user experience study used interviews with the hospital's own health workers as its research site, not a signed partnership.

content.text: Rumah Sakit Semen Gresik, a hospital in Gresik, East Java, became the subject of a 2021 user experience study rather than a formal partner in one. Researchers used the hospital's plan to offer care at home as a real world design problem, interviewing its own healthcare workers along the way.

The paper, "Perancangan User Experience Pada Aplikasi Mobile HomeCare Rumah Sakit Semen Gresik Menggunakan Metode Design Thinking," is listed in MGM's publication registry and credited to Isadora, Hanggara, and Mursityo. It describes the hospital's interest in letting patients receive certain services without visiting in person, an idea that mattered more as the pandemic changed how people used hospitals and how comfortable they felt sitting in a waiting room. The research team followed a design thinking process, moving from empathizing with hospital staff and patients through defining the core problem, sketching ideas, and building prototypes, to sketch two linked mobile applications, one aimed at patients booking home visits and one aimed at the hospital's own home care staff managing their schedules. The designs were then checked with a standard user experience questionnaire completed by people who tried them, a common way to score how usable and appealing an interface feels before it is built for real.
Where the hospital's name comes from

The hospital's name traces back to Semen Gresik, the cement company long associated with the city. Public company profiles describe Rumah Sakit Semen Gresik as run by PT Cipta Nirmala, a body connected to today's Semen Indonesia Group, though that corporate lineage is separate from the 2021 research and did not itself involve MGM. The study treated the hospital purely as a healthcare provider with an operational problem to solve, not as a corporate sponsor.

props.caption: The Semen Indonesia headquarters in Gresik, East Java. The cement company's name lives on in Rumah Sakit Semen Gresik. Image: Consigliere Ivan, CC BY 2.0.

content.text: None of this points to an ongoing arrangement between the hospital and MGM. What the record shows is a single applied study: real interviews with hospital staff, a real operational problem brought on by a difficult year for healthcare providers, and a design proposal tested with real users, the kind of grounded, unglamorous research that MGM's publication registry exists to hold.
Source: https://mgm.ub.ac.id/index.php/mgm/home/publication and https://j-ptiik.ub.ac.id/index.php/j-ptiik/article/view/8496

article.title: A 2022 Paper Links MGM to LIPI's Machine Learning Group
article.subtitle: A study on teaching basic programming paired a Universitas Brawijaya researcher with a scientist from LIPI, the institute later folded into BRIN.

content.text: In 2022, a study on how vocational school students learn basic programming brought together researchers from two different corners of Indonesian science. One worked at Universitas Brawijaya's computer science faculty. The other was based at the Indonesian Institute of Sciences, known by its Indonesian initials LIPI, in a research group built around machine learning.

The paper, titled "An Interactive Learning Environment System on Basic Programming Subjects: Effects of Learning Outcomes and Question Level Patterns," appeared in JTEV, a journal of electrical and vocational engineering published in Padang. It tested a teaching system built around problem posing and problem solving exercises, tried out with 36 vocational school students split evenly into an experimental group and a control group. Herman Tolle, of Universitas Brawijaya's Media, Game, and Mobile Technologies research group, the group known on campus as MGM, coauthored the paper with Ahmad Afif Supianto, listed under LIPI's Machine Learning Research Group, Research Center for Informatics. Two more coauthors, from a polytechnic in Banjarmasin and a university in Japan, rounded out the author list.
From LIPI to BRIN

LIPI's Machine Learning Research Group no longer exists under that name today. In 2021, Indonesia folded LIPI and several other science agencies into one body, the National Research and Innovation Agency, known as BRIN. The 2022 paper still lists Supianto under LIPI, which places this coauthorship at the tail end of LIPI's existence rather than describing any current arrangement between MGM and BRIN.

props.caption: The Tugu UB monument on the Universitas Brawijaya campus in Malang. Image: Fajar Embun, CC BY-SA 3.0.

content.text: The study itself was modest in scope, a classroom intervention measured against a control group at a single vocational school, tracking how students answered questions of different difficulty levels as they worked through the material. It is, on its own terms, a real and citable instance of an MGM researcher publishing alongside a scientist from Indonesia's national research institute, worth recording precisely rather than dressed up as something larger.
Source: https://ejournal.unp.ac.id/index.php/jtev/article/view/113579 and https://mgm.ub.ac.id/index.php/mgm/home/publication

article.title: Rebuilding a CAT Exam System for BKPSDM Kabupaten Malang
article.subtitle: A FILKOM UB community service team spent months reconfiguring a Moodle based testing platform directly inside Malang Regency's own exam laboratory.

content.text: Malang Regency's civil service agency runs its promotion and recruitment exams on its own computers, and by 2024 the system behind those exams badly needed an overhaul.

The Badan Kepegawaian dan Pengembangan Sumber Daya Manusia Pemerintah Kabupaten Malang, known as BKPSDM Pemkab Malang, administers Computer Assisted Test, or CAT, exams from its own dedicated CAT laboratory. A community service team from Fakultas Ilmu Komputer, Universitas Brawijaya, made up of three lecturers, Agi Putra Kharisma, Aryo Pinandito, and Eriq Muhammad Adams Jonemaro, along with seven Informatics Engineering students, took on the project starting in May 2024. This kind of hands on, applied community service activity is the sort of work regularly carried out by FILKOM's Media, Game and Mobile Technology (MGM) laboratory community.
Built Where the Exams Happen

The team's first phase involved interviews with BKPSDM staff, including computer systems officers, who described specific problems with the existing setup: it could not handle image based or essay questions, could not weight scores differently per question, could not randomize questions and answers, and sometimes confused participants who shared the same name. To address this, the team turned to Moodle, a platform they already knew well from Universitas Brawijaya's own BRONE e-learning system. On September 19, 2024, they traveled to BKPSDM's own CAT laboratory in Malang Regency to configure the software directly on site, working with an architecture of one server serving roughly 40 client computers. Because the lab's server ran Windows, the team used WampServer to run Apache, PHP, and MySQL together.

props.caption: A school computer lab with rows of desktop workstations, illustrating the kind of setup a Moodle based computer assisted testing system runs on. Image: Felix An, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: After configuration came deployment and testing, to confirm the new setup actually worked under real conditions. Agi Putra Kharisma, who led the team, reported that the activity went smoothly and surfaced new ideas that could feed into future community service work with the agency. For the research community around Lab MGM at FILKOM, the project is a concrete example of applied, on the ground collaboration with a local government partner, built through direct development work rather than a signed cooperation agreement.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2024/10/09/pengembangan-program-cat-di-bkpsdm-pemkab-malang-oleh-filkom-ub/ and https://dimasloka.ub.ac.id/index.php/dimasloka/article/download/43/28

article.title: A Researcher at Two Universities Links UM and MGM
article.subtitle: A Universitas Negeri Malang researcher has repeatedly coauthored Kit-Build concept mapping studies with MGM, a research coauthorship rather than a signed institutional partnership.

content.text: Didik Dwi Prasetya holds appointments at both Universitas Negeri Malang and Hiroshima University, and that dual footing has made him a recurring coauthor on concept mapping research alongside MGM's Aryo Pinandito.

Their clearest joint paper is "Design and Development of Semi-Automatic Concept Map Authoring Support Tool," published in Research and Practice in Technology Enhanced Learning in 2021, coauthored by Pinandito, Prasetya, and Hiroshima University's Yusuke Hayashi and Tsukasa Hirashima. The paper describes a tool that helps teachers build Kit-Build concept maps, a format where students reconstruct a concept map from a set of provided pieces rather than drawing one from scratch, and the study looked at ways to make authoring those maps less time consuming for instructors.
A research line that keeps going

The same core group, MGM's Pinandito together with Hiroshima University's Hayashi and Hirashima, kept publishing Kit-Build research in the years after. A 2024 paper in the same journal, "Evaluating the Kit-Build Concept Mapping Process Using Sub-Map Scoring," proposed a way to score the smaller sub-maps a student builds along the way, not just their finished map, as a closer measure of how well they actually understood the material. Its other coauthors, Ridwan Rismanto and Banni Satria Andoko, are affiliated with Politeknik Negeri Malang, a separate Malang institution covered elsewhere on this site, rather than with Universitas Negeri Malang.

props.caption: Image: Uliyanti, CC BY-SA 4.0. Malang, East Java, seen from Paralayang hill, home to Universitas Negeri Malang.

content.text: It is worth being precise about the shape of this connection. Prasetya's coauthorship with Pinandito is a real, repeated research relationship, documented across more than one paper in the same journal, but it is a tie between two researchers and their Hiroshima University collaborators, not a signed agreement between Universitas Negeri Malang and MGM as institutions. Universitas Negeri Malang itself is a public university historically focused on teacher education, a natural fit for Prasetya's interest in classroom tools like concept mapping.

For MGM, the connection to Universitas Negeri Malang, through Prasetya's work with Pinandito, shows how a single research interest, here making concept maps easier to build and score, can sustain a coauthorship across years and multiple papers without ever needing a formal institutional partnership behind it.

Source: https://rptel.apsce.net/index.php/RPTEL/article/view/2024-19021 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373937832_Evaluating_the_kit-build_concept_mapping_process_using_sub-map_scoring and https://rptel.apsce.net/index.php/RPTEL/article/view/2021-16008

article.title: Universitas Narotama Tours Lab MGM
article.subtitle: A 37 person delegation from Surabaya explored Lab MGM's research up close, though the visit produced networking rather than a signed agreement.

content.text: In May 2026, a group of 37 visitors from Surabaya spent time walking through FILKOM's laboratories, including the one behind much of the faculty's mobile and game related research.

The delegation came from the Faculty of Computer Science at Universitas Narotama Surabaya, and FILKOM UB hosted them for a program that included presentations on the faculty's flagship initiatives and a tour of several research laboratories. Lab MGM, short for Media, Game and Mobile Technology, was one of the labs the visitors explored directly, looking at the kind of research and student projects the group produces, work that over the years has touched on mobile applications, assistive technology, and location based systems, among other areas.
A Visit, Not a Signed Partnership

FILKOM UB described the event as a way to strengthen academic networking and collaboration between the two institutions. No MGM specific agreement, memorandum of understanding, or joint project was reported to have come out of the visit itself. Visits like this are a routine part of how Indonesian universities build relationships with each other, giving a delegation a close look at labs, facilities, and research output well before any formal cooperation is discussed, if it ends up being discussed at all. For Lab MGM, hosting a delegation of this size is a way of putting its work in front of another institution, even when no concrete partnership follows right away.

props.caption: Surabaya City Hall, in the city home to Universitas Narotama. Image: consigliere ivan, CC BY-SA 2.0.

content.text: Whether this particular visit leads to a future joint project between Universitas Narotama and FILKOM UB, or with Lab MGM specifically, is not yet known and nothing of that kind has been announced. What is documented is the visit itself: a sizeable delegation, a faculty wide presentation, and a direct look inside Lab MGM's work, all framed by FILKOM as relationship building rather than as the signing of any agreement.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2026/05/28/terima-kunjungan-universitas-narotama-surabaya-filkom-ub-paparkan-berbagai-program-unggulan/

article.title: How Lab MGM Helped Build UB Tanggap COVID-19
article.subtitle: In early 2020, Lab MGM joined its own university's task force, IT unit, and planning department to launch an app tracking campus health during the pandemic.

content.text: When Indonesia recorded its first COVID-19 cases in March 2020, Universitas Brawijaya needed a fast way to know how thousands of students, lecturers, and staff across campus were doing.

The university's answer was UB Tanggap COVID-19, an application launched in early April 2020 that combined a self screening questionnaire with location tracking and health status monitoring for the entire campus community, referred to at UB as the civitas academica. Building it was not the work of a single team. It brought together Universitas Brawijaya's COVID-19 Prevention Task Force, the university's Information and Computer Technology Unit, the Urban and Regional Planning Department at the Faculty of Engineering, and Lab MGM, short for Media, Game and Mobile Technology, at the Faculty of Computer Science.
What the App Actually Did

After a user filled in the self screening form, the system analyzed the responses and sorted people into categories based on risk. Anyone flagged as a patient under observation saw contact information for the university's task force hotline appear immediately, and the task force could follow up by text message. The app also logged each user's location at the point of registration and included a list of nearby hospitals, giving both individuals and the university a clearer, faster picture of health conditions across campus during a period when in person monitoring was difficult to organize.

props.caption: The main gate of Universitas Brawijaya in Malang, East Java. Image: Lorrainevyu, CC BY 4.0.

content.text: UB Tanggap COVID-19 is not an example of Lab MGM partnering with an outside organization. It is Lab MGM working alongside other units of its own university, Universitas Brawijaya, to respond to a fast moving public health emergency. That internal, cross unit collaboration, spanning a task force, an IT unit, an engineering department, and a computer science lab, shows how Lab MGM's development work has, at times, served the university that houses it directly, rather than an external partner.

Source: https://teknik.ub.ac.id/2020/04/track-the-civitas-condition-ub-launches-ub-tanggap-application/?lang=en and https://surabaya.bisnis.com/read/20200407/531/1223793/universitas-brawijaya-luncurkan-aplikasi-lacak-sivitas-antisipasi-corona and https://seru.co.id/12939-aplikasi-ub-tanggap-mampu-lacak-keberadaan-kondisi-kesehatan-sivitas/amp

article.title: 16 Students at Universitas Andalas Tested a Rehabilitation Exergame
article.subtitle: A 2025 study on hand gestures for rehabilitation games ran its experiment with student participants in Padang, not as a coauthoring institution.

content.text: When researchers needed real hands to test a set of gestures for a rehabilitation video game, they turned to Universitas Andalas in Padang, West Sumatra. Sixteen students there took part in the experiment, making the university a research site and a source of participants rather than a listed coauthoring institution.

The 2025 paper, "An Investigation of Hand Gestures for Controlling Video Games in a Rehabilitation Exergame System," was written by Radhiatul Husna, Komang Candra Brata, Irin Tri Anggraini, Nobuo Funabiki, Alfiandi Aulia Rahmadani, and Chih Peng Fan. An exergame is a video game built around physical movement rather than a controller, an approach that fits naturally with rehabilitation exercise, where patients need to repeat specific motions in a way that holds their attention. The team used hand tracking software to test candidate gestures for controlling such a game, narrowing a pool of 32 possible simple gestures down to 10 judged easiest for patients to perform without strain. The 16 Universitas Andalas students helped the team evaluate which of these gestures felt natural, comfortable, and accessible during actual use.
A research site, not a coauthor

Universitas Andalas does not appear among the paper's listed institutional affiliations. Its role in the record is the experiment itself: a group of students willing to sit through rounds of gesture trials for a rehabilitation tool being developed elsewhere, giving the researchers real, varied feedback on what a patient recovering from an injury might actually find manageable. That is a narrower claim than a research partnership, and it is the accurate one.

props.caption: The rectorate building at Universitas Andalas in Padang, West Sumatra. Image: SpartacksCompatriot, CC BY 3.0.
The library at Universitas Andalas. Image: Rahmat Irfan Denas, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: For MGM, the study is a reminder that research contributions take different shapes. Sometimes it is a coauthor's name on a paper, and sometimes it is a group of students in Padang, willing to spend an afternoon testing hand gestures for a game built to help someone else's recovery.
Source: https://www.mdpi.com/2073-431X/14/1/25 and https://scholar.ub.ac.id/en/publications/an-investigation-of-hand-gestures-for-controlling-video-games-in-/

article.title: Tokopedia's UX Designer Opens Lab MGM's Interaction Design Series
article.subtitle: Lab MGM invited Tokopedia UX Designer Labina Kirby to open its 2022 Interaction Design guest lecture series, sharing her design career journey with FILKOM students.

content.text: In February 2022, Lab MGM, the Media, Game, and Mobile Technology Laboratory at Fakultas Ilmu Komputer, Universitas Brawijaya, invited Labina Kirby, a UX Designer at Tokopedia, to open its Webinar Series on Interaction Design, a guest lecture program built around FILKOM alumni working in industry.

Kirby, a 2015 graduate of FILKOM's Information Systems program, joined the session on February 11, 2022, alongside Faisal Risq Efendy, a Product Designer at tiket.com. Around 180 students attended the online talk, titled Road to Product (UX) Designer: Building Your Design Career Journey, moderated by faculty member Hanifah Muslimah Az-zahra. That turnout made it the best attended session of the four Lab MGM would go on to run that year. The two spoke about moving from a computer science degree into working UX design roles at Indonesian technology companies.
What the Session Covered

As with the rest of the series, Kirby took part as an individual invited guest, sharing her own career experience rather than representing any formal arrangement between Tokopedia and Lab MGM. She told students that critical thinking and a creative mindset matter as much as technical skill for anyone hoping to work in UX design, describing the daily work of solving usability problems and collaborating across product, engineering, and business teams.

props.caption: Jakarta's business district. Image: Shubhi Rofiddinsa, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: Tokopedia is an Indonesian e-commerce platform connecting merchants with buyers across the country. For FILKOM students weighing where a computer science degree might lead, hearing from an alumna who had made that jump gave the opening session of the series a concrete, personal starting point.

props.caption: A person shopping online from a laptop. Image: Bogdan Hoyaux, CC BY 4.0.

content.text: Kirby's talk set the tone for a four part series that Lab MGM ran through much of 2022. The sessions that followed covered UX strategy from an industry perspective, emotional design, and basic AI for game and user interaction, with each guest invited individually and a certificate offered to students who registered and attended.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/02/10/webinar-series-on-interaction-design-sesi-1-road-to-product-ux-designer/ and https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/02/24/road-to-product-ux-designer/

article.title: tiket.com's Product Designer Shares His Career Path at Lab MGM
article.subtitle: Lab MGM invited Faisal Risq Efendy, a Product Designer at tiket.com, to speak alongside a Tokopedia designer in the first session of its 2022 Interaction Design series.

content.text: On February 11, 2022, Lab MGM, the Media, Game, and Mobile Technology Laboratory at Fakultas Ilmu Komputer, Universitas Brawijaya, welcomed Faisal Risq Efendy, a Product Designer at tiket.com, as a guest speaker in its Webinar Series on Interaction Design, a guest lecture program built around FILKOM alumni working in industry.

Efendy, a 2016 graduate of FILKOM's Informatics Engineering program, appeared alongside Labina Kirby, a UX Designer at Tokopedia, for the series' opening session, Road to Product (UX) Designer: Building Your Design Career Journey. Around 180 students joined the online event over Zoom, moderated by faculty member Hanifah Muslimah Az-zahra, making it the best attended of the four sessions Lab MGM would run that year.
What the Session Covered

Efendy took part as an individual alumnus invited to share his own professional path. He told students that networking matters from the very start of a career, encouraging them to use competitions, internships, and research projects to build experience and professional connections while still studying. He walked through his own route from a computer science degree at FILKOM to product design work at an Indonesian online travel platform that handles flight, train, and hotel bookings.

props.caption: Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Jakarta's main gateway for domestic and international travel. Image: Hullie, CC BY-SA 3.0.

content.text: His participation gave students a second, contrasting view of what a design career can look like outside e-commerce, in a company built around travel rather than retail. The session closed with a question and answer segment where students asked both speakers about portfolios, interviews, and the move from student projects to product work.

props.caption: Jakarta, home to many of Indonesia's technology and travel companies. Image: Shubhi Rofiddinsa, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: Efendy's talk was the first of four sessions Lab MGM ran across 2022 under the same series, each pairing new invited guests with new topics: UX strategy from an industry perspective, emotional design, and basic AI for game and user interaction followed over the rest of the year, with certificates made available to students who registered and attended.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/02/10/webinar-series-on-interaction-design-sesi-1-road-to-product-ux-designer/ and https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/02/24/road-to-product-ux-designer/

article.title: Saga University's Long Running Research Line With MGM
article.subtitle: A Saga University professor has repeatedly coauthored e-learning and virtual reality research with MGM researchers, a recurring coauthorship rather than a signed partnership.

content.text: Kohei Arai, a professor at Saga University in Japan, has coauthored research with MGM's Herman Tolle, Aryo Pinandito, and Eriq M. A. Jonemaro for over a decade, a working relationship that runs through shared academic interests rather than a formal agreement between the two universities.

The collaboration traces back to around 2014 and 2015, when the two groups worked together on e-learning and virtual reality research. One paper from that period, "Virtual Reality Game Controlled with User's Head and Body Movement Detection Using Smartphone Sensors," carries all four names, Tolle, Pinandito, Jonemaro, and Arai, and describes a smartphone based virtual reality game that a player controls by walking, turning, and moving their head while wearing a simple cardboard headset, rather than by pressing buttons. The work fit naturally alongside Tolle's long running interest at MGM in delivering virtual reality through ordinary smartphones instead of specialized hardware.
A relationship traced through MGM's own registry

MGM keeps an internal registry of its publications, and this particular collaboration is documented there. A live public copy of the paper was not reachable while preparing this article, so its precise venue and page numbers are reported here based on how the paper is catalogued across academic indexes rather than from a copy read directly. What is clear and worth stating plainly is the shape of the relationship: a multi year pattern of coauthorship between Arai at Saga University and Tolle's group at MGM, centered on e-learning and virtual reality research, not an institutional partnership between the two universities.

props.caption: Image: Pekachu, CC BY-SA 4.0. The front gate of Saga University's Honjo Campus in Saga, Japan.

content.text: Saga University is a national university on Japan's Kyushu island, with faculties spanning science and engineering, agriculture, medicine, and education. Arai himself is known for coauthoring widely with universities across Southeast Asia on topics in remote sensing, computer vision, and applied information science, of which the work with MGM is one long running example.

props.caption: Image: Pekachu, CC0. Saga city, seen looking toward the Saga University campus.

content.text: For MGM, the tie to Saga University shows how a lab's research network can grow through one prolific coauthor's interests rather than a top down agreement, with individual projects accumulating over years into a genuine, if informal, working relationship.

Source: https://mgm.ub.ac.id/index.php/mgm/home/publication and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/285614376_Virtual_reality_game_controlled_with_user's_head_and_body_movement_detection_using_smartphone_sensors

article.title: PENS Joins MGM's Look at Augmented Reality Navigation
article.subtitle: A researcher from Politeknik Elektronika Negeri Surabaya coauthored a 2023 study on outdoor AR navigation with MGM, a research coauthorship rather than an institutional agreement.

content.text: A 2023 study comparing how smartphones handle augmented reality navigation apps put researchers from MGM and Politeknik Elektronika Negeri Surabaya, commonly known as PENS, on the same author list.

The paper, "An Investigation of Running Load Comparisons of ARCore on Native Android and Unity for Outdoor Navigation System Using Smartphone," was presented at the 2023 International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering, held in Surabaya that October. Its authors include MGM's Komang Candra Brata as corresponding author, PENS researcher Sritrusta Sukaridhoto, Nobuo Funabiki, Evianita Dewi Fajrianti, and Mustika Mentari.
Comparing two ways to build the same app

The study built the same outdoor navigation prototype twice, once directly in native Android and once in the Unity game engine, both using Google's ARCore toolkit to place directional markers over the real world as seen through a phone's camera. The team then measured which approach ran lighter and faster outdoors. Native Android came out ahead on raw performance and resource use in outdoor conditions, while Unity kept its usual advantages for teams that need to support multiple platforms or build with complex 3D assets. The result is a practical guide for developers choosing between the two approaches, rather than a verdict that one is simply better.

It is worth stating plainly what this relationship is and is not. Sukaridhoto's contribution reflects one researcher joining a specific study alongside Brata and collaborators, not a cooperation agreement between PENS and MGM as institutions. PENS itself is a state polytechnic in Surabaya focused on electronics and informatics engineering education, distinct from and located in a different city than MGM's home at Universitas Brawijaya in Malang.

props.caption: Image: Rifky2011, CC BY 4.0. Surabaya, East Java, home to Politeknik Elektronika Negeri Surabaya.

content.text: Small studies like this one rarely make headlines, but they are how a lab's research network actually grows in practice, one shared technical problem and one visiting coauthor at a time, well short of any formal institutional tie.
Source: https://scholar.ub.ac.id/en/publications/an-investigation-of-running-load-comparisons-of-arcore-on-native-/ and https://cir.nii.ac.jp/crid/1874242817219228928

article.title: A Taiwan Professor Joins MGM's Rehabilitation Gaming Research
article.subtitle: Chih Peng Fan of National Chung Hsing University coauthored a 2025 study on hand gestures for rehabilitation exergames with MGM's Komang Candra Brata.

content.text: A 2025 paper on rehabilitation video games carries a coauthor list that stretches from Malang to Taichung. Among the six names is Chih Peng Fan, a professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering at National Chung Hsing University in Taiwan, working alongside MGM's Komang Candra Brata.

The paper, "An Investigation of Hand Gestures for Controlling Video Games in a Rehabilitation Exergame System," published in January 2025, looked for hand gestures that patients in physical rehabilitation could perform comfortably while playing a video game built around hand tracking software rather than a physical controller. The team tested a pool of 32 possible gestures, weighing how easy each one was to learn and repeat, and settled on 10 judged easiest to use for people recovering from injury or limited mobility. The experiment's participants were 16 students at Universitas Andalas in Padang, a separate relationship from Fan's coauthorship and covered on its own elsewhere on this site.
A genuine coauthor, not a partner institution

Fan has spent more than two decades on the electrical engineering faculty at National Chung Hsing University, working on digital image processing, pattern recognition, and embedded system design, the kind of background that fits naturally with a project tracking hand movement through a camera. His role on this paper is a real research coauthorship rather than an institutional agreement between two universities. Nothing in the paper suggests National Chung Hsing University itself holds any formal tie to MGM beyond Fan's individual contribution to this one study alongside Komang Candra Brata.

props.caption: The library at National Chung Hsing University in Taichung, Taiwan. Image: Ralff Nestor Nacor, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: It is a small, specific kind of connection: one researcher, one paper, one shared interest in helping rehabilitation patients play games with gestures their bodies can actually manage. That is worth stating plainly, in its true modest scale, rather than inflating it into something it was never meant to be.
Source: https://www.mdpi.com/2073-431X/14/1/25 and https://scholar.ub.ac.id/en/publications/an-investigation-of-hand-gestures-for-controlling-video-games-in-/

article.title: A Taiwan Professor and MGM's Decade of Augmented Reality Research
article.subtitle: Researchers at MGM and National Central University in Taiwan coauthored augmented reality navigation studies together across several years, a research link rather than a signed partnership.

content.text: In 2015, a study on augmented reality bus navigation connected two computer science labs on opposite sides of the South China Sea: MGM at Universitas Brawijaya in Indonesia and National Central University in Taiwan.

The link ran through two researchers. MGM's Komang Candra Brata and National Central University's Deron Liang coauthored "Location-Based Augmented Reality Information for Bus Route Planning System" together with Sholeh Hadi Pramono. It was published in the International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering, volume 5, issue 1, pages 142 to 149. The paper described an Android application that overlays a live camera view with directional markers, guiding a rider on foot toward the nearest bus stop and helping them judge which route to take in an unfamiliar part of a city.
A research link that kept going

This was not a one time exchange. According to MGM's own publication record, Brata and Liang went on to coauthor further papers together in 2019 and 2020, extending the same line of location based augmented reality research across several years. It is worth being precise about what this means. No institutional memorandum of understanding between MGM and National Central University is on file here, and what the record actually shows is a recurring coauthorship between two individual researchers, not a formal partnership agreement signed between the two universities.

props.caption: Image: Mnb, CC BY-SA 3.0. A campus building at National Central University in Jhongli, Taoyuan, Taiwan.

content.text: National Central University is a public research university based in Jhongli, a district of Taoyuan City, tracing its roots to a school founded in Nanjing in 1915 before reestablishing itself in Taiwan in the 1960s. It is known today for strengths in electrical engineering, atmospheric science, and space and remote sensing, the kind of engineering department that gave Liang the background to work on a location based mobile application with a partner in Indonesia.

props.caption: Image: Person Lin, CC BY-SA 2.0. A view across the National Central University campus in Jhongli.

content.text: For MGM, the tie to National Central University is a reminder that a lab's international footprint is often built one coauthored paper at a time, through individual researchers finding common ground on a shared technical problem, well before, or entirely apart from, any formal agreement between their institutions.
Source: https://ijece.iaescore.com/index.php/IJECE/article/view/5627 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272760699_Location-Based_Augmented_Reality_Information_for_Bus_Route_Planning_System

article.title: Visits and Ties with NTU's Centre for Augmented and Virtual Reality
article.subtitle: Lab MGM leaders have visited Singapore's CAVR twice, in 2019 and 2022, to learn from and discuss cooperation with one of the region's AR and VR research centres.

content.text: The Centre for Augmented and Virtual Reality, known as CAVR, sits within Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. It is an intercollege centre that combines education and training with research in AR and VR, and it operates in partnership with the technology provider EON Reality. Lab MGM's leadership has visited CAVR on two occasions, in 2019 and again in 2022, in what has so far been a relationship of visits and discussion rather than a signed bilateral agreement between MGM and NTU.
Two visits, several years apart

NTU's own records note that a delegation from Universitas Brawijaya visited CAVR on April 18, 2019, where the visitors were shown the centre's range of AR and VR equipment and given an explanation of CAVR's role within NTU. Lab MGM leadership was among those who took part in that trip.

props.caption: The administration building and Tan Chin Tuan Lecture Theatre at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore. Image: Kenrick95, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: Lab MGM returned to CAVR in December 2022, this time as part of a broader trip through Singapore aimed at initiating cooperation with international university and industry partners around the interactive media stream that Lab MGM manages within FILKOM's curriculum. FILKOM's own writeup frames the visit as an initiation of cooperation and a look at curriculum improvement, language that points to an early-stage relationship rather than a finalized partnership agreement.

It was through this same CAVR connection that Lab MGM's delegation was introduced to EON Reality, the centre's industry partner, and to the AR, VR, and XR discussions that followed on that trip. CAVR functions here as the bridge between an Indonesian research group and Singapore's wider AR and VR ecosystem, more than as a partner MGM has a direct agreement with.

That distinction matters for how this relationship should be read. CAVR is a university facility that hosts visiting delegations from many institutions, and being shown its equipment or introduced to its partners is not the same as holding a joint research agreement with NTU. What the two visits do show is a sustained interest, spanning several years, in learning from a well established regional centre before committing Lab MGM to any specific line of AR or VR work of its own.

FILKOM's and NTU's own accounts consist of two documented visits, in 2019 and 2022, each described in terms of exchange and initiation rather than a signed cooperation agreement between Lab MGM and NTU.

Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/12/22/inisiasi-kerjasama-dan-perbaikan-kurikulum-filkom-ub-kunjungi-cavr-ntu-dan-fxmedia-singapura/ and https://www.ntu.edu.sg/cavr/news-events/news/news-detail/brawijaya-university and https://www.ntu.edu.sg/cavr

article.title: Mister Aladin's Lead Developer Talked Emotional Design at Lab MGM
article.subtitle: Lab MGM invited Fathin Naufal Hawi, Lead UI/UX Developer at Mister Aladin, to speak in the third session of its 2022 Interaction Design guest lecture series.

content.text: On May 20, 2022, Lab MGM at Fakultas Ilmu Komputer, Universitas Brawijaya held the third session of its Webinar Series on Interaction Design, a guest lecture program built around FILKOM alumni working in industry, with Fathin Naufal Hawi, Lead UI/UX Developer at Mister Aladin, as one of two guest speakers.

Hawi, a 2013 graduate of FILKOM's Information Systems program, joined Dara Adhelia, a UI Designer at Blibli, for a session titled UX Design: Emotional Design, moderated by faculty member Agi Putra Kharisma. Roughly 70 students attended the online talk, the smallest audience of the three 2022 sessions with confirmed attendance figures, in which both speakers discussed how emotion shapes the way people experience digital products.
What the Session Covered

Hawi took part as an invited alumnus with relevant industry experience, not as a representative of any partnership between Mister Aladin and Lab MGM. Mister Aladin is an Indonesian travel and hotel booking platform, and his work there centers on the interfaces travelers use to search for and book places to stay. In the session, he and Adhelia discussed how attractive, well considered design creates positive emotional responses in users, and how that emotional layer shapes whether people keep using a product.

props.caption: A hotel lobby in Palembang, Indonesia. Image: Firzafp, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: For a booking platform, that might mean the difference between a traveler feeling reassured while confirming a room and one who abandons the process out of doubt. The talk gave FILKOM students a practical view of UI and UX development inside a travel technology company, where trust and reassurance carry real weight.

props.caption: Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Jakarta's main gateway for domestic and international travel. Image: Hullie, CC BY-SA 3.0.

content.text: The session closed out the middle stretch of a four session series that Lab MGM ran through most of 2022, following earlier talks from speakers at Tokopedia, tiket.com, Blibli, and Mekari. Each guest, Hawi included, was invited individually as a working professional and alumnus, not as part of any lasting arrangement between Mister Aladin and Lab MGM.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/05/23/mengetahui-minat-masyarakat-dan-konsumen-melalui-emotional-design/

article.title: Jagoan Indonesia, a 2016 Pilot Project with Mirai Education
article.subtitle: Long before recent partnerships, the MGM Research Group launched an educational app about Indonesian culture built with guidance from Japan's Mirai Education.

content.text: In May 2016, the MGM Research Group launched Jagoan Indonesia, an educational app for children built around Indonesian provinces, landmarks, and traditional culture, from the MGM room at FILKOM. It is one of the older entries in Lab MGM's history of outside collaboration, and it points to a relationship with a Japanese educational technology company called Mirai Education.
A pilot project under Mirai's guidance

FILKOM described Jagoan Indonesia explicitly as a pilot project produced through cooperation between FILKOM and Mirai Education, with development carried out under Mirai's guidance. Mirai Education's apps were, at the time, popular in Japan and ranked among the top titles in the education category of the Apple App Store, which is part of why FILKOM sought the company out as a production partner for its own first attempt at a culture focused learning app.

props.caption: The National Monument in Jakarta, one of the many Indonesian landmarks that this kind of cultural education app is built around. Image: Ramayoni, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: Herman Tolle, a senior figure in the MGM Research Group, described himself around this period as director of the Mirai Indonesia Education Project, which suggests the relationship extended beyond this one app into a broader, ongoing effort branded under the Mirai Indonesia name. The available record does not give a full picture of how large or how long running that broader project was, so this page treats Jagoan Indonesia as the clearest, best documented product of the relationship rather than assuming everything the Mirai Indonesia name covered.

A decade on, Jagoan Indonesia is a historical rather than an active partnership. It is included here because it shows that Lab MGM's interest in working with outside companies on educational technology did not start with the more recent visits and agreements described elsewhere in Lab MGM's partner history. It started, at least in part, with a children's app about Indonesia built alongside a Japanese studio in 2016.

FILKOM's own account does not describe the Mirai relationship continuing as a formal, ongoing partnership past this period. What the app does establish is a working method that shows up again in Lab MGM's later international contacts, learning production or research practices from a more experienced outside partner on a specific, bounded project, rather than entering into an open ended cooperation from the start.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2016/05/20/filkom-ub-luncurkan-aplikasi-edukasi-kebudayaan-dan-kekayaan-indonesia/

article.title: Mekari's UX Researcher Spoke on Strategy at Lab MGM's Second Session
article.subtitle: Lab MGM invited Verrel Radiman, a UX Researcher at Mekari, to join the second session of its 2022 Interaction Design guest lecture series.

content.text: On March 11, 2022, Lab MGM, the Media, Game, and Mobile Technology Laboratory at Fakultas Ilmu Komputer, Universitas Brawijaya, held the second session of its Webinar Series on Interaction Design, with a guest speaker from Mekari, an Indonesian business software company that builds accounting, HR, and tax products.

Verrel Radiman, then a UX Researcher at Mekari and a FILKOM Informatics Engineering student from the 2017 cohort, joined Vivy Junita, a Product Manager at Blibli, for a session titled Defining The Impactfulness Of UX Strategy: Industry Perspective. About 90 students attended online, moderated by faculty member Adam Hendra Brata.
What the Session Covered

Radiman took part as an invited individual with direct industry experience, sharing what UX research looks like day to day rather than representing any agreement between Mekari and Lab MGM. He walked students through the UX researcher role, describing empathy, organization, and critical thinking as the core qualities needed to understand user needs and spot opportunities in a product. He and Junita both stressed that UX strategy has to flex with a company's product development approach rather than follow one fixed process.

props.caption: A shared office workspace. Image: Crew, Unsplash, CC0 1.0.

content.text: Mekari builds accounting, HR, and tax software used by businesses across Indonesia, a different kind of product from the consumer marketplaces most other speakers in the series represented. That gave students a look at UX research inside enterprise software, a field that gets less classroom attention than consumer app design but plays a similar role in whether a product succeeds.

props.caption: Jakarta's business district. Image: Shubhi Rofiddinsa, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: The session was the second of four Lab MGM ran under the same series across 2022, following a February session with speakers from Tokopedia and tiket.com and preceding a May session on emotional design with speakers from Blibli and Mister Aladin. Each guest, including Radiman, was invited individually for a single conversation rather than through any ongoing arrangement with their employer.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/10/07/sertifikat-webinar-series-on-interaction-design/ and https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/03/18/mendefinisikan-dampak-strategi-ux-dari-perspektif-dunia-industri/

article.title: Lab MGM and Kyutech's Assistive Technology Exchange
article.subtitle: In 2018, Lab MGM's researchers presented alongside Kyushu Institute of Technology's Chikamune Wada, inside a wider, faculty level FILKOM partnership with Kyutech.

content.text: In October 2018, a professor from Japan stood in front of FILKOM students to talk about wheelchairs that respond to head movements and devices that let people with limited speech communicate through a screen.

Professor Chikamune Wada of the Kyushu Institute of Technology, known as Kyutech, in Kitakyushu, Fukuoka, traveled to Fakultas Ilmu Komputer, Universitas Brawijaya, for a guest lecture titled Introduction of Assistive Research for Disabled and Elderly, held on Thursday, October 18, 2018. The session opened with a presentation from Fitri Utaminingrum, head of FILKOM's Computer Vision research group, on a smart wheelchair that could be controlled five different ways, including manually, by remote control, by voice command, by head movement, or automatically by following a guide walking ahead of it.
Lab MGM's Part in the Program

The second presentation came from Herman Tolle, head of FILKOM's Media, Game and Mobile Technology (MGM) research group, who described MGM's own work on disability and elderly related technology, including indoor location estimation, user activity recognition, and a head movement control system called HEMOCS. He highlighted iHelp, a head worn device built on HEMOCS that lets users with limited mobility or speech select words with head movements and have them spoken aloud. Prof. Wada closed the session with an overview of assistive technology research worldwide and his own studies on crutch walking mechanics and public bus accessibility for blind passengers in Thailand.

props.caption: The General Educational Building on the Tobata campus of Kyushu Institute of Technology in Kitakyushu, Japan. Image: Kugel, public domain.

content.text: This lecture sat inside a broader, growing relationship between FILKOM and Kyutech, one that led FILKOM to sign an institutional memorandum of understanding with Kyutech the following year, in 2019, with exchange and research cooperation continuing since. That MoU is a faculty level agreement between FILKOM and Kyutech as a whole, not a separate contract held by Lab MGM on its own. Lab MGM's connection to Kyutech runs through moments such as this guest lecture, where its researchers present alongside Kyutech's own faculty inside that wider institutional relationship, rather than through a bilateral agreement of its own.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2018/10/23/kuliah-tamu-introduction-of-assistive-research-for-disabled-and-elderly/

article.title: Building Sarjana Sakti with PT Indogetjob
article.subtitle: Lab MGM helped build a mobile job fair portal that pairs Brawijaya graduates with employers through a soft skills assessment.

content.text: When the COVID-19 pandemic forced Indonesia's offline job fairs to shut down, unemployment among young graduates climbed sharply, and Universitas Brawijaya's computer science faculty set out to build a digital alternative.

The result was Sarjana Sakti, short for Akses Cari Kerja Sarjana Terintegrasi, a mobile job fair portal that lets fresh graduates complete a soft skills assessment and get matched with employers without submitting a formal application. The app was launched on January 8, 2022, alongside Universitas Brawijaya's 59th anniversary, and its creator, Dr. Eng. Herman Tolle, was at the time FILKOM's Deputy Dean for Academic Affairs. The launch was funded through a Kedaireka matching fund program run by Indonesia's Directorate General of Higher Education, which paired FILKOM lecturers with industry partners on several projects that year.
A Named, Direct Collaboration

Sarjana Sakti's development is credited explicitly in a paper published in Universitas Brawijaya's Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer, which states that the Media, Game and Mobile Technology (MGM) Laboratory at FILKOM collaborated directly with PT Indogetjob International Solution to build the platform. PT Indogetjob's chief executive, Iwan Nazarudin, took part in the launch event as the industry collaborator, describing the assessment system as a way to surface the leadership and teamwork qualities that employers look for when hiring. The paper also describes how researchers used a Human-Centered Design approach, testing the interface with real users across several iterations before release, and reported strong usability and user experience scores from that testing.

props.caption: An information kiosk at a job fair in Malang, Indonesia, the kind of offline event Sarjana Sakti was built to complement online. Image: Cyosce, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: Graduates who complete the assessment are recommended to local, regional, national, and even international companies, in principle opening doors that would otherwise require a formal application process. The platform remains reachable at sarjanasakti.com. For Lab MGM, Sarjana Sakti stands as one of its clearer examples of a named, direct partnership with an outside company, built around a concrete shared product rather than a single event or a one time visit.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/01/13/ub-launching-aplikasi-sarjana-sakti-karya-dosen-filkom/ and https://jtiik.ub.ac.id/index.php/jtiik/article/download/6770/pdf/27801

article.title: Lab MGM and Hiroshima University Sign a Research Fellowship Agreement
article.subtitle: An Implementation Agreement links FILKOM's Lab MGM with Hiroshima University's Learning Engineering Laboratory for joint research on digital concept maps.

content.text: In 2024, Fakultas Ilmu Komputer Universitas Brawijaya signed an Implementation Agreement on Research Fellowship with the Graduate School of Advanced Science and Engineering at Hiroshima University in Japan. It is, by most measures, the strongest formal academic tie that Lab MGM has built with a partner outside Indonesia.
A joint research group on learning technology

The agreement set up an international research group chaired by Aryo Pinandito, who was head of Lab MGM at the time. On the Indonesian side, FILKOM describes the collaboration as involving the Sistem Informasi study program together with Lab MGM, working opposite Hiroshima's Learning Engineering Laboratory. According to FILKOM, the three units jointly provide research assistance, run experiments, and support publication of results, rather than one side simply hosting visiting researchers from the other.

props.caption: The Higashi Hiroshima campus of Hiroshima University, home to the Graduate School of Advanced Science and Engineering. Image: Taisyo, CC BY 3.0.

content.text: The research theme that has anchored the partnership is the Kit-Build Concept Map, a digital concept mapping method developed by the Learning Engineering Laboratory to help teachers assess how well students understand a topic. FILKOM reports that the two sides continued this line of work into 2025, this time aimed at building predictive models that estimate a learner's intelligent understanding and progress from that concept map data, and that the continuation was again formalized through an Implementation Agreement rather than an informal arrangement.

A concept map is, in simple terms, a diagram that lays out how a set of ideas connect to each other. The Kit-Build variant asks a student to build their own map from a fixed kit of pieces, then compares it against a map built by an instructor, which gives a teacher a fast, structured read on where a student's understanding is thin. Turning that comparison into a predictive model, one that can flag likely gaps in understanding before a test does, is the kind of applied learning technology research that sits naturally alongside Lab MGM's broader interest in educational media and games.

For Lab MGM, the relationship is notable less for any single output and more for its structure. It is described by FILKOM as a standing agreement covering multiple years of joint work, not a one-time exchange visit, which puts it in a different category from most of the international contacts documented elsewhere in Lab MGM's partner history. Even so, this account is limited to what FILKOM has published about the agreement and its 2025 continuation, and does not go beyond that.

Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2024/09/30/kolaborasi-riset-internasional-melalui-implementation-agreement-on-research-fellowship-fakultas-ilmu-komputer-universitas-brawijaya-dengan-graduate-school-of-advanced-science-and-engineering-hiroshima/ and https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2025/10/28/filkom-ub-dan-hiroshima-university-laksanakan-pengembangan-predictive-model-intelligent-learning-pada-media-pembelajaran-berbasis-peta-konsep-digital-kit-build-concept-map/

article.title: A Singapore Conversation with fxMedia on AR, VR, and the Metaverse
article.subtitle: Lab MGM leaders visited the Singapore based studio fxMedia in 2022 to talk about immersive media technology, a discussion rather than a signed partnership.

content.text: fxMedia is a Singapore based studio working in immersive media, and it is the kind of company Lab MGM's leadership sought out during a December 2022 trip built around initiating cooperation with international partners in the interactive media field.
What the visit covered

Aryo Pinandito, then head of Lab MGM, and Herman Tolle, head of the MGM Research Group, visited fxMedia as part of a wider Singapore itinerary that also took in NTU's Centre for Augmented and Virtual Reality. FILKOM's account of the trip refers to fxMedia as an international industry partner and describes the conversation there as covering virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality, extended reality, and metaverse technology.

props.caption: Singapore's Central Business District skyline, the setting for Lab MGM's 2022 industry visits. Image: Nicolas Lannuzel, CC BY-SA 2.0.

content.text: Alongside the technology discussion, the two sides explored the possibility of collaborative research in AR, VR, and metaverse topics. FILKOM's writeup describes this as an exploration of shared interests rather than a finished project, and there is no record of a signed research or partnership agreement resulting from the meeting.

It is worth noting that the metaverse and immersive media space was moving quickly in 2022, with universities and studios across the region trying to work out where their interests overlapped. A visit like this one served that purpose for FILKOM: a chance to hear directly from a studio actually building AR and VR products, rather than to walk away with a concrete deliverable. Nothing in FILKOM's account suggests the conversation went further than that.

For Lab MGM, the value of the fxMedia conversation lay in exposure to how a working immersive media studio approaches the same technologies the lab teaches and researches, and in laying groundwork that could inform future curriculum or research decisions around the interactive media stream. FILKOM's account stands as a record of an industry visit and discussion rather than of an active or ongoing collaboration.
Source: https://filkom.ub.ac.id/2022/12/22/inisiasi-kerjasama-dan-perbaikan-kurikulum-filkom-ub-kunjungi-cavr-ntu-dan-fxmedia-singapura/

article.title: Meeting EON Reality Through NTU's CAVR Network
article.subtitle: A 2022 Singapore meeting with EON Reality led to talk of pursuing an MoU for an AR and VR centre at Universitas Brawijaya, though no final agreement is documented.
