The requirement list came out of the journey map, not a feature request.

When the prototype was tested, the strongest signal was on the monitoring question, where the wearable scored far above the phone. The usability scores overall stayed close, and travel time fell. The method, in other words, did not just produce a nicer app. It produced a correct diagnosis of what was slow.

For teams working on public services, the transferable lesson is the order of the work. Talk to riders, draw the journey, name the pain points and only then decide what to build. The authors note that twenty participants is a small sample and treat the results as preliminary.
Source: Brata et al. (2021). Usability improvement of public transit application through mental model and user journey. TELKOMNIKA Telecommunication, Computing, Electronics and Control. DOI:

article.title: Mengapa Guru Butuh Alat Permainan Edukatif yang Dirancang Khusus
article.subtitle: Merancang permainan untuk anak usia dini menuntut tiga hal sekaligus: aturan, jalannya permainan, dan rasa senang.

content.text: Alat permainan edukatif sudah menjadi bagian dari kelas taman kanak-kanak sejak lama. Namun alat yang ada tidak selalu selaras dengan kompetensi yang diminta kurikulum, terutama di sekolah dengan fasilitas pembelajaran menengah ke bawah. Kesenjangan inilah yang menggerakkan sebuah penelitian di JTIIK.
Berangkat dari kompetensi kurikulum

Peneliti memulai dengan menelusuri kompetensi inti dan kompetensi dasar untuk siswa kelompok A, yaitu anak usia empat sampai lima tahun. Dari sana mereka menetapkan satu sasaran yang sempit dan terukur, bukan seluruh materi pengenalan angka sekaligus.
Sasaran materinya adalah pengenalan angka 1 sampai 10.
Anak diharapkan mengenali nama, bentuk, dan nilai dari setiap angka.
Bentuknya permainan papan, supaya anak belajar sambil bergerak dan berbicara, bukan menatap layar.

props.caption: Papan permainan ular tangga bergaya lama. Image: Wellcome Collection, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Tiga lapisan yang harus dipikirkan

Perancangan memakai kerangka MDA. Kerangka ini memaksa perancang membedakan apa yang ia tulis di aturan, apa yang benar-benar terjadi saat anak bermain, dan perasaan apa yang muncul dari situ. Ketiganya sering dianggap sama, padahal tidak.
Mechanics: aturan main, seperti cara melempar dadu dan berpindah petak.
Dynamics: perilaku yang muncul ketika aturan itu dijalankan anak-anak.
Aesthetics: rasa senang, penasaran, dan tantangan yang dirasakan pemain.

props.caption: Anak-anak bermain di taman kanak-kanak. Foto: State Government Photographer, CC0.

content.text: Pengembangan berjalan iteratif sampai delapan putaran, dan setiap putaran mengubah aturan main. Hasil akhirnya dimainkan dua siswa dengan satu narator, peran yang diisi guru. Guru memegang kendali cerita, sementara anak-anak yang mengambil keputusan di papan. Pembagian peran itu membuat alat ini tetap bisa dipakai di kelas dengan satu pendamping.

Sumber: Abdiel Wahyu Ramadhyono, Eriq Muhammad Adams Jonemaro, dan Tri Afirianto (2024). Perancangan Gim Edukasi Anak Usia Dini untuk Meningkatkan Pemahaman Pengenalan Angka. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: Measuring Diopters with a Phone Camera
article.subtitle: A prototype turns the distance between a face and a screen into an estimate of refractive error.

content.text: A diopter is the unit that describes the strength of a lens. People with myopia usually know their prescription exists, but few know what value it currently sits at, because the tools that measure it are clinical equipment. A 2019 paper in TELKOMNIKA proposed a different route: let a smartphone estimate the number.
Working from the blur line

The concept rests on a simple observable event. A person with myopia holds text at a comfortable distance, then slowly moves the phone closer until the letters stop being sharp. That point is the blur line. If the phone knows how far away the face is at that moment, it can convert the distance into a diopter value.
Face to screen distance is computed from the base length between the two eyes, following a method published by Konig and colleagues.
The Google Mobile Vision API locates the left eye, right eye, and nose, and only the phone's own sensors and front camera are used.

props.caption: A patient reading a Snellen chart, the standard way to check vision. Image: Beendy234, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The range the method covers

The distance method only works between 19 and 89 centimetres. That ceiling becomes a floor and a ceiling for the result, so the application can estimate from about minus 1.12 to minus 5.26 diopters. The user measures the right eye first with the left closed, then repeats the steps for the left eye.

props.caption: Corrective lenses, the treatment the app is meant to support. Image: Jacek Halicki, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: What the usability test showed

Five participants tested the prototype, chosen using the common five user rule for usability work. They completed every task without failure and finished in an average of 2.03 minutes. The modified System Usability Scale gave a total score of 80.5, which counts as usable, with participants rating the language, instructions, and interface consistency highest.

The weakest item, at 2.20, was whether the result matched the participant's actual condition. Some users saw a different diopter value than their real prescription, which the authors list as a limitation and a subject for the next study.

Source: Komang Candra Brata and Mukhammad Sharif Hidayatulloh (2019). An idea of intuitive mobile diopter calculator for myopia patient. TELKOMNIKA (Telecommunication Computing Electronics and Control). DOI:

article.title: Why Reusing Lecture Recordings Is Harder Than It Looks
article.subtitle: A conversion layer between old course material and new devices beats rewriting content from scratch.

content.text: Every institution keeps a shelf of digital teaching material that nobody can open anymore. The files are intact. The software that produced them is not.
A 2014 study looked at this problem and proposed a way to bring old composite e-learning content to smartphones. The interesting part is not the specific tooling. It is the pattern the authors chose.
Convert at the edge, not at the source

Instead of asking lecturers to rebuild their material for mobile, the method places a conversion layer between the old content and the new device. That layer does the messy work: reading the original package, converting media formats, and serving the result as a web service that a phone application can open.

props.caption: Recorded lectures outlive the software that made them. Photo: Heidy Garcia, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Three properties make that pattern worth copying.
The original files stay untouched, so nothing is lost if the conversion has to be redone later with better tools.
The conversion runs as a service, so supporting a new device or format means updating one component instead of revisiting the content itself.
The output is checked against a real audience. The study reported a usability acceptance score of 94% rather than assuming that a working conversion is a good experience.

props.caption: Desktop era courseware, the kind this pipeline rescues. Photo: LeanForward lf, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: There is a limit worth naming. A pipeline like this preserves what the original content did. It does not fix material that was poor to begin with, and it does not redesign a lecture that was never suited to a small screen.

props.caption: Adapted content still has to land with students. Photo: Esthee2010, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Even so, the economics are hard to argue with. Extraction and transcoding are jobs a machine can do reliably and repeatedly. Rewriting a decade of course material by hand is a job that usually never gets started.

Source: Herman Toile, Kohei Arai, and Aryo Pinandito (2014). Adaptation of composite E-Learning contents for reusable in smartphone based learning system. 2014 International Conference on Advanced Computer Science and Information Systems. DOI:

article.title: What Two Routing Algorithms Teach Us About Transit Apps
article.subtitle: Choosing a routing method is a trade off between time, memory, and the phones your users actually carry.

content.text: Choosing an algorithm for a product is rarely about which one is mathematically better. It is about which cost you are willing to pay, on the hardware your users actually carry.

A 2023 study compared two ways of recommending public transit routes: the long established Dijkstra algorithm and ant colony optimization, which mimics how ants find short paths. The goal was not to crown a winner, but to see whether the newer method could match the older one under the same conditions.
Pick your metric before your algorithm

The team tracked computation time and memory consumption, including how much memory each method held at the start and at the end of a run. Those two numbers are usually what decides whether a feature feels smooth on a mid range phone.

props.caption: Graph analysis software visualising a large network. Image: SlvrKy, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Three habits from this study are worth copying into your own benchmarks.
Establish ground truth first. The team ran Dijkstra to define the best route, then asked the competing method to match it. Without that reference, a faster result proves nothing.
Measure repeatedly. A single reading hides variance, while repeated runs expose the real spread of results.
Record the trade off, not just the win. Ant colony optimization came out ahead on execution time and on the number of pathways traversed, but the findings suggest it needs a larger memory budget.

props.caption: Transit systems can be modelled as layered networks. Image: Martin Grandjean, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The measurement discipline here is easy to underestimate. Running the same test many times protects against one off artifacts, and the researchers call out the garbage collector specifically. In a managed runtime, memory behaviour during a single run can be an accident of timing rather than a property of the algorithm.

props.caption: Public minivans at a terminal in Malang. Photo: Mujiono Ma'ruf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: For teams building transit features, the practical advice is to define what you are optimising for before writing the code. If memory is scarce, the classic algorithm is a safe default. If you are searching a very large network and can afford the footprint, the ant based approach deserves a test on your own data.

Source: Abdul Jabbar and Aryo Pinandito (2023). Recommending Public Transit Route: Ant-Colony Optimization or Dijkstra? 2023 International Conference on Modeling and E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications. DOI:

article.title: Why Language Apps Avoid Speaking Practice
article.subtitle: Vocabulary and reading fit neatly on a screen. Listening and speaking need a microphone, a voice, and a commitment to designing both.

content.text: Open a language app and you mostly see the same three activities. Flash cards for vocabulary, quizzes for grammar, and passages for reading. These are the parts of language learning that translate cleanly into taps and swipes.

Listening and speaking translate less cleanly. They need audio, a microphone, and a way to judge whether the learner said something close to the right thing. That is why a team at Universitas Brawijaya found the same gap across existing Japanese apps, and built Hanasu to fill it.
The design problem behind the idea

Pronunciation is not an add-on in Japanese. It is part of the foundation, and a learner who never speaks aloud carries a weakness no amount of vocabulary drilling fixes. Skipping it in software is a choice born of convenience, not pedagogy.

props.caption: Turning a spoken word into a system signal is its own engineering problem. Credit: IHEARu, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: The team's answer leans on text to speech for the listening half, which turns written content into audio without a recording booth. The speaking half converts the learner's voice into a lesson interaction. Both moves reuse infrastructure that already exists rather than building a speech lab from scratch.
Lessons for anyone building this
Start from users, not from the feature list. The team gathered requirements from students and lecturers before writing the lesson flow.
Compare interface options in public. A and B testing decided which controls made sense, which matters more on a phone than on a desktop.
Follow multimedia learning principles. Pairing illustration, text and audio deliberately is different from placing them on a screen together.
Report preliminary results as preliminary. The evaluation was small scale, and the authors frame the outcome as feasibility rather than proof.

props.caption: In a classroom the speaking partner is a teacher. On a phone it must be designed. Credit: Mosborne01, CC BY-SA 3.0.

content.text: The broader point reaches past Japanese. Any skill that needs a voice runs into the same wall, and the apps that clear it will have an advantage that flash cards cannot copy. The work is unglamorous: microphones, feedback, and testing on real devices.

Source: Komang Candra Brata, Adam Hendra Brata and Eko Prasetyo Lukman (2019). Hanasu: Interactive Japanese language m-learning application to support listening and speaking exercise. Proceedings of the 2019 3rd International Conference on Education and Multimedia Technology (ICEMT 2019), 311-315. DOI:

article.title: Membaca Beban Kognitif Lansia dari Gerakan Mata
article.subtitle: Studi ini memakai eye-tracking dan kuesioner NASA TLX untuk melihat kaitan fixation dengan beban kognitif saat lansia memakai aplikasi.

content.text: Pengguna lansia memakai aplikasi perpesanan dan media sosial setiap hari. Kendala mereka sering diringkas jadi soal ukuran huruf atau kontras warna. Padahal ada pertanyaan yang lebih dasar: seberapa besar beban kognitif yang mereka tanggung, dan bisakah beban itu dibaca dari cara mata mereka bergerak?

Dua peneliti dari Universitas Brawijaya mencoba menjawabnya. Mereka merekam gerakan mata pengguna lansia dengan eye-tracker, lalu membandingkan data itu dengan skor beban kognitif yang dilaporkan sendiri oleh responden.
Cara penelitian dijalankan

Eye-tracking dipilih karena tidak invasif, sehingga cocok untuk responden lanjut usia. Untuk mengukur beban kognitif, penulis memakai NASA Task Load Index, kuesioner baku yang memecah beban kerja jadi lima dimensi: tuntutan mental, tuntutan temporal, kinerja, usaha, dan frustrasi.

Dari sisi mata, penulis mengambil dua variabel: fixation count, yaitu berapa kali mata berhenti pada satu titik, dan fixation duration, yaitu berapa lama mata berhenti. Setiap dimensi NASA TLX diuji terpisah terhadap kedua variabel itu memakai korelasi Spearman.

props.caption: Alat pelacak gerak mata. Foto: Rai S G Bari, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Hasil yang muncul

Pola paling konsisten muncul pada fixation count. Jumlah fixation berkorelasi positif dengan tuntutan mental, usaha, dan frustrasi, dengan kekuatan rendah sampai kuat. Artinya, makin sering mata berhenti, makin berat beban yang dirasakan. Sebaliknya, fixation count berkorelasi negatif lemah dengan kinerja.

Untuk fixation duration, penulis menemukan dua korelasi positif berkekuatan sedang, yaitu dengan usaha dan frustrasi. Lama mata berhenti ternyata lebih erat terkait dengan rasa lelah dan jengkel daripada dengan tuntutan mental itu sendiri.

props.caption: Warga lansia memakai telepon pintar. Foto: Zheongugbulld, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Penulis menutup dengan catatan penting: hubungan antar variabel ini tidak berdiri sendiri. Rancangan tugas, keahlian dan kebiasaan lansia, serta desain aplikasi ikut memengaruhi hasil. Karena itu eye-tracking diusulkan sebagai salah satu indikator tuntutan mental, bukan ukuran tunggal, untuk mengarahkan perbaikan antarmuka yang lebih ramah lansia.

Sumber: Prasojo dan Pinandito (2024). Korelasi Fixation Dan Beban Kognitif pada Pengguna Lansia Dengan Eye-Tracking Pada Aplikasi Komunikasi dan Media Sosial. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: Membuat Navigasi Angkutan Kota Malang Lebih Ringan
article.subtitle: Kompresi data dan penyederhanaan graf memangkas waktu pencarian rute sekaligus menghemat kuota pengguna.

content.text: Aplikasi navigasi transportasi umum sering terasa lambat di ponsel kelas menengah. Peta rute menyimpan ribuan titik koordinat, dan setiap titik ikut dihitung ketika pengguna meminta rekomendasi perjalanan.

Tim peneliti dari Universitas Brawijaya membangun aplikasi Android yang merekomendasikan rute angkutan umum di Kota Malang. Jaringan trayek dimodelkan sebagai graf, lalu algoritme Dijkstra mencari jalur terpendek antara dua halte. Pertanyaan penelitiannya sederhana: bagaimana membuat proses itu lebih cepat dan lebih hemat kuota?
Tiga komponen yang diuji
Eksperimen memisahkan tiga komponen supaya efek masing-masing bisa diukur sendiri.
Format JSON sebagai media pertukaran data antara server dan aplikasi.
Kompresi data memakai Zlib yang dikombinasikan dengan encoding Base64.
Penyederhanaan graf secara visual memakai algoritme Douglas Peucker.

props.caption: Angkot trayek GM di Terminal Mulyorejo, Malang. Foto: Mujiono Ma'ruf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Kompresi terbukti menghemat bandwidth. Mengirim data dalam format JSON efektif, dan kombinasi Zlib dengan Base64 memangkas penggunaan bandwidth untuk distribusi data di internet sebesar 64,61%. Beban tambahan pada memori server hanya 0,44%, jadi harga yang dibayar jauh lebih kecil daripada penghematannya.

props.caption: Papan informasi trayek angkutan kota Malang. Foto: Mujionomaruf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Efek penyederhanaan graf

Perubahan terbesar datang dari penyederhanaan graf. Setelah titik yang dianggap tidak penting dibuang, waktu yang dibutuhkan untuk merekomendasikan rute turun 81,24% dan penggunaan memori berkurang 72,99%. Inilah alasan aplikasi peta terasa jauh lebih responsif ketika data rute dirapikan lebih dulu.

props.caption: Angkutan umum melintasi Taman Gadang, Malang. Foto: Mujiono Ma'ruf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Bagi pengembang aplikasi transportasi, urutan langkahnya cukup jelas: rapikan dulu datanya, baru hitung rutenya. Kedua teknik ini bisa dipakai bersama tanpa mengubah algoritme pencarian jalur, sehingga risikonya kecil dan hasilnya langsung terasa di perangkat pengguna.

Sumber: Pinandito et al. (2024). Peningkatan Performa Komputasi Sistem Navigasi Transportasi Publik Pada Perangkat Bergerak Melalui Penerapan Teknik Kompresi Data Dan Penyederhanaan Graf. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: KNN untuk Deteksi Risiko Diabetes pada Kehamilan
article.subtitle: Model sederhana dengan akurasi 78 persen dari data Puskesmas Lawang.

content.text: Diabetes yang muncul atau sudah ada sebelum kehamilan membawa risiko besar. Ibu hamil dengan gangguan keseimbangan glukosa lebih rentan mengalami preeklampsia, kelahiran prematur, plasenta previa, sampai hipoglikemia pada bayi yang baru lahir. Karena itu, penapisan awal menjadi penting, terutama di fasilitas kesehatan yang sumber dayanya terbatas.
Dari mana datanya berasal

Tim peneliti memakai 248 catatan pemeriksaan ibu hamil di Puskesmas Lawang, Kabupaten Malang, dari Januari sampai Agustus 2021. Setiap catatan memuat 16 atribut, mulai dari usia ibu, usia kehamilan, riwayat kehamilan, indeks massa tubuh, sampai hasil skrining hepatitis, HIV, dan infeksi menular seksual.
Atribut yang dipakai mencakup GPA (gravida, para, abortus), riwayat penyakit, faktor risiko, dan riwayat persalinan sebelumnya.
Kelas yang diprediksi adalah status risiko tinggi atau tidak pada kehamilan tersebut.

props.caption: Alat ukur glukosa darah untuk memantau kadar gula. Foto: Roy Zuo, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Empat skenario pengujian

Metode yang dipilih adalah K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). Algoritma ini menebak kelas sebuah data baru dengan melihat seberapa dekat data itu ke tetangga terdekatnya. Tim menguji empat nilai k dan membandingkan beberapa rasio pembagian data latih dengan data uji.
k=2 menghasilkan akurasi tertinggi 70,27 persen.
k=3 naik menjadi 75,68 persen.
k=4 memberi hasil terbaik, 78,38 persen.
k=5 sedikit menurun ke 77,03 persen.

props.caption: Pemantauan kehamilan menangkap risiko lebih awal. Foto: Goleisureintl, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Rasio 7:3 antara data latih dan data uji memberi hasil terbaik pada hampir semua skenario. Artinya, model lebih stabil ketika porsi data untuk belajar cukup besar, sementara sisanya tetap cukup untuk menguji.

Angka 78,38 persen jelas belum cukup untuk menggantikan penilaian bidan atau dokter. Namun hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa catatan pemeriksaan rutin di puskesmas sudah cukup kaya untuk memberi sinyal awal, asalkan atributnya diisi lengkap dan konsisten.

Sumber: Aryo Pinandito, Satrio Agung Wicaksono, dan Satrio Hadi Wijoyo (2023). Implementasi Machine Learning Dalam Deteksi Risiko Tinggi Diabetes Melitus Pada Kehamilan. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: Kenapa Pengelompokan Membuat Pencarian Citra Lebih Cepat
article.subtitle: Membandingkan gambar baru dengan seluruh isi basis data itu mahal, dan klaster memangkas pekerjaan itu.

content.text: Bayangkan mencari satu foto di dalam lemari berisi ratusan gambar, satu per satu. Itulah yang dilakukan komputer pada pencarian citra yang paling sederhana. Setiap gambar di basis data dibandingkan dengan gambar kueri, dan cara ini benar tetapi lambat, karena biaya waktunya tumbuh seiring bertambahnya koleksi.

props.caption: Transformasi wavelet kontinu. Gambar: DaBler, domain publik, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Sebuah penelitian menempuh jalan pintas yang rapi. Sebelum pencarian, seluruh koleksi dikelompokkan lebih dulu memakai K-Means. Sistem hanya perlu membandingkan gambar kueri dengan tiap pusat klaster, memilih klaster terdekat, lalu memeriksa isi klaster itu saja. Pekerjaan pembandingan berkurang drastis.
Ciri gambar dan ukuran kemiripannya

Sebelum bisa dikelompokkan, gambar harus diubah menjadi angka. Di sini Haar wavelet transform dipakai untuk mengekstrak ciri, yaitu menangkap pola penting pada gambar dalam bentuk yang jauh lebih ringkas. Kemiripan antar gambar kemudian dihitung dengan ukuran jarak F-Norm.
Koleksi uji berisi 500 gambar dalam lima kategori: dinosaurus, bus, pantai, kuda, dan bunga.
Presisi meningkat sekitar 40 persen dibandingkan pencarian tanpa pengelompokan.
Waktu temu kembali menjadi 1,6 sampai 2,7 kali lebih cepat.

props.caption: Model model temu kembali informasi. Gambar: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.

content.text: Ada satu parameter yang menentukan hasilnya, yaitu ambang batas kemiripan untuk menghentikan pencarian. Ambang yang terlalu ketat membuat sistem terus memeriksa, sedangkan ambang yang terlalu longgar membuat hasilnya asal-asalan. Penelitian ini menguji tiga nilai dan menemukan bahwa kategori kuda mendapat keuntungan terbesar, dengan presisi 51 persen lebih baik pada ambang 0,5.

Kategori yang lebih seragam menunjukkan pola berbeda. Untuk dinosaurus, sistem mencapai recall 1,00 dengan presisi 0,25 dalam 3,80 detik, lalu berubah menjadi presisi 0,99 dalam 1,48 detik setelah pengelompokan diterapkan. Perubahan itu bukan sekadar lebih cepat, tetapi juga jauh lebih tepat.

Batas penelitian ini perlu disebut. Basis datanya kecil, 500 gambar dengan lima kategori yang isinya sudah jelas, jadi jumlah klaster yang pas belum tentu lima pada koleksi nyata. Foto sehari-hari yang bercampur dalam banyak topik akan menuntut penanganan berbeda. Yang bisa dibawa pulang adalah prinsipnya: susun data sebelum mencari, dan biaya pencarian akan menyusut dengan sendirinya.
Sumber: Jonemaro dan Rusdianto (2016). Sistem Temu Kembali Citra Berbasis Konten Menggunakan Haar Wavelet Transform Dan K-Means Clustering. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: Kemudahan Pakai Jadi Kunci Aplikasi Kuliner Halal
article.subtitle: Ketika 64 wisatawan menilai aplikasi pelacak kuliner halal, faktor kemudahan bergerak lebih dulu.

content.text: Ada anggapan lama dalam pengembangan aplikasi: kalau fiturnya cukup banyak, pengguna akan datang sendiri. Sebuah studi tentang aplikasi pelacak kuliner halal menunjukkan urutan yang berbeda. Sebelum menilai manfaat sebuah aplikasi, pengguna lebih dulu menilai apakah aplikasi itu gampang dipakai.

props.caption: Label halal jadi informasi pertama yang dicari wisatawan. Foto: Emna Mizouni, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Rantai pengaruh yang terukur

Model yang diuji menyusun empat variabel secara berurutan: persepsi kemudahan, persepsi kemanfaatan, minat menggunakan, dan penggunaan nyata. Setiap hubungan diuji dengan t tabel 1,669. Kemudahan berpengaruh nyata terhadap kemanfaatan dengan t hitung 6,820, angka tertinggi kedua setelah jalur minat menuju penggunaan nyata yang mencapai 10,517.
Kemudahan ke kemanfaatan: t hitung 6,820
Kemudahan ke minat: t hitung 2,037
Kemanfaatan ke minat: t hitung 5,389
Minat ke penggunaan nyata: t hitung 10,517

Jalur terlemah justru yang paling menarik dibahas. Kontribusi kemudahan terhadap minat hanya 0,237, artinya 72,3 persen variasi minat dijelaskan oleh indikator lain. Rasa mudah saja tidak cukup untuk membuat orang berniat memakai aplikasi, karena manfaat yang terlihat ikut menentukan.

props.caption: Peta kuliner halal berguna kalau benar-benar dipakai. Foto: Gunawan Kartapranata, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Pelajaran untuk perancang aplikasi

Satu indikator dibuang dari model. Pernyataan mudah diingat hanya memperoleh loading factor 0,498, sedikit di bawah ambang 0,50. Responden menilai aspek itu kurang penting, sehingga tim mengeluarkannya dari perhitungan. Yang dianggap penting bukan menghafal cara pakai, melainkan aplikasi yang langsung bisa digunakan.
Pastikan pencarian lokasi bisa diselesaikan dalam beberapa langkah saja
Uji kemudahan dengan pengguna dari luar kota dan tunjukkan manfaat nyata lewat informasi menu

Penerimaan pengguna secara umum baik. Nilai predictive relevance 0,885 menunjukkan model ini menggambarkan kondisi lapangan dengan baik. Rata-rata jawaban responden berada di angka 4 dari skala setuju, dan wisatawan memang menantikan alat seperti ini. Aplikasi wisata kuliner bersaing dengan banyak pilihan lain di ponsel, dan yang bertahan adalah aplikasi yang tidak membuat penggunanya berpikir dua kali sebelum membukanya.
Sumber: Sucipto Sucipto dkk. (2019). Analisis Penerimaan Aplikasi Tracking Kuliner Halal oleh Wisatawan di Kabupaten Malang. Jurnal Sosioteknologi. DOI:

article.title: Teaching Japanese Language Apps to Talk Back
article.subtitle: A mental model study and an A/B test compare a conversational m-learning design with the apps students already use.

content.text: Most Japanese learning apps on the market do the same three things well: reading, vocabulary, and writing. Speaking and listening sit at the edge, even though conversation is the point of learning a language. A 2020 study in IJECE set out to design a version that puts both back at the centre.
Reading the learner's mental model

The team started with a diary study involving 20 respondents, split between students and teachers who already knew basic hiragana. The goal was to capture a mental model, the internal picture a person carries about how a task works. Personas and a user journey map turned those notes into requirements.
Learners wanted pronunciation practice and a way to check whether they got it right.
The learning flow should feel like a conversation rather than a quiz queue.

props.caption: A hiragana chart covering basic, voiced, and combined characters. Image: TealComet, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Putting two versions side by side

The design was tested with A/B testing, also called split testing. Twenty high grade students with similar backgrounds used both the proposed app and an existing Japanese m-learning app, then answered the short version of the User Experience Questionnaire.

props.caption: A kana chart, the material most learners start from. Image: W-dcem, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: What participants reported
On the practical side, the two apps came out nearly level, with the existing app slightly ahead on perspicuity, efficiency, and dependability. The gap opened on the experiential side.
Pragmatic quality: existing app 2.23, proposed app 2.15 on a scale from -3 to 3.
Hedonic quality: proposed app 1.45 against -0.44 for the existing one.

The authors conclude that combining speaking and listening exercises in multimedia content gives a better overall experience, while warning that learning outcomes were not measured, so the design should not yet be credited with better results.

Source: Komang Candra Brata and Adam Hendra Brata (2020). User experience improvement of japanese language mobile learning application through mental model and A/B testing. International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering. DOI:

article.title: Yang Perlu Dipahami Perancang Aplikasi untuk Lansia
article.subtitle: Data gerakan mata bisa menunjuk bagian antarmuka yang membebani, jauh sebelum pengguna menyampaikan keluhan.

content.text: Keluhan pengguna lansia sering datang terlambat, yaitu setelah mereka berhenti memakai aplikasinya. Metrik klasik seperti waktu penyelesaian tugas dan tingkat keberhasilan bisa terlihat baik saja, padahal pengguna menanggung beban mental yang tidak terlihat.

Penelitian ini menawarkan indikator tambahan yang muncul lebih awal: gerakan mata. Eye-tracker dapat merekam berapa kali dan berapa lama pandangan berhenti di satu titik pada layar, tanpa mengganggu pengguna.
Kenapa fixation layak diperhatikan

Hasil pengujian menunjukkan jumlah fixation berkorelasi positif dengan tuntutan mental, usaha, dan frustrasi. Ini masuk akal: area antarmuka yang membingungkan membuat mata berkali kali kembali ke tempat yang sama. Sebaliknya, fixation count berkorelasi negatif dengan kinerja, jadi makin sering pandangan berbalik, makin rendah hasil yang dicapai.

Durasi fixation memberi sinyal yang berbeda. Korelasi sedang muncul pada usaha dan frustrasi, bukan pada tuntutan mental. Jadi lama pandangan berhenti lebih menandakan kelelahan dan kejengkelan pengguna.

props.caption: Lansia memakai telepon pintar di ruang publik. Foto: Zheongugbulld, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Yang bisa dilakukan perancang
Uji antarmuka dengan pengguna lansia, bukan hanya dengan pengguna muda.
Periksa area yang menarik pandangan berulang kali, karena di situ beban menumpuk.
Sederhanakan alur dan kurangi jumlah keputusan dalam satu layar.

props.caption: Rangkaian eye-tracking di laboratorium. Foto: Naomi Nota, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Penulis juga mengingatkan bahwa beban yang terukur dipengaruhi banyak hal di luar desain aplikasi: jenis tugas, tingkat keahlian, dan kebiasaan lansia memakai perangkat. Dua responden bisa menghasilkan pola mata berbeda untuk aplikasi yang sama.

Karena itu temuan ini paling berguna sebagai bahan pembanding. Rekam data mata sebelum dan sesudah perbaikan antarmuka, lalu lihat apakah jumlah fixation pada area bermasalah benar benar turun. Itu bukti yang lebih meyakinkan daripada tanggapan subjektif saja.

Sumber: Prasojo dan Pinandito (2024). Korelasi Fixation Dan Beban Kognitif pada Pengguna Lansia Dengan Eye-Tracking Pada Aplikasi Komunikasi dan Media Sosial. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: How tightly students connect a new concept map to an old one
article.subtitle: A study measured the links that span between two maps, and found a wide gap between two teaching techniques.

content.text: Concept mapping is a familiar classroom activity. Students put concepts in boxes, join them with labelled arrows, and end up with a diagram of what they understand. Extension concept mapping adds a second step: students take a map they already built and extend it using new material.

The interesting part is not either map on its own. It is the links that cross between them. The researchers call these extension relationships, or ER, and treat them as a signal of how well a learner has integrated new knowledge with what they already knew.

props.caption: A concept map about concept maps. Boxes hold concepts, labelled arrows hold meaning. Image: Dvitalo12, CC BY-SA 3.0.

content.text: How the experiment was set up

The team worked with 55 second year university students in a Database 1 course covering relational databases. Both classes were tested beforehand and found comparable. One class of 27 became the control group using an open ended extension method. The other class of 28 used a Kit-Build approach, recomposing a map from components the teacher supplies.
Phase one: 25 minutes on the original material, then build the first map.
Phase two: 25 minutes on additional material, then 15 minutes to extend the earlier map.

props.caption: A student working at a computer. Both groups built their maps digitally. Photo: woodleywonderworks, CC BY 2.0.

content.text: What the numbers showed

The gap between the groups was large on both measures. Students using the Kit-Build method produced far more connecting propositions, and those propositions scored much higher on a four level quality rubric that graded how sound the underlying understanding was.
Quantity of extension relationships: 1.63 on average for the control group against 5.32 for the Kit-Build group.
Quality of extension relationships: 3.74 against 14.43 on the same comparison.
Both differences were statistically significant, with p values below 0.001 and large effect sizes.

The authors credit the structure of the activity. When a learner recomposes a teacher's map, they begin from an organised knowledge structure instead of a blank canvas. Extending that structure gives new material something solid to attach to. They also flag clear limits: a small sample, a single class meeting, and conditions that were not fully identical for both groups. The finding is offered as preliminary.

Source: Prasetya, D.D., Pinandito, A., Hayashi, Y., et al. (2021). Investigating the Tightness of Connection between Original Map and Additional Map in Extension Concept Mapping. Proceedings of the International Conference on Computers in Education (ICCE 2021).

article.title: Practice Feedback That Works Without a Mentor
article.subtitle: The design story behind a Hijaiyah learning prototype that scores pronunciation on a scale.

content.text: Practice only improves when the learner gets feedback. In Quran reading, that feedback has traditionally come from a person who can hear the letter and correct it on the spot. The research team behind a Hijaiyah mobile learning prototype asked a practical question: how much of that loop can a phone carry on its own?
Start from the learner

Before writing any scoring code, the team ran a field study with five participants who were already comfortable with Android apps and had tried Iqro level 1. They built personas and a user journey map to capture where the existing apps lost people.
Participants wanted a rating between 0 and 100, not a pass or fail verdict.
They wanted to speak directly to the app without extra setup steps.

props.caption: Reading the Quran, the skill a mentor normally checks. Image: Rezasfllh, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Calibration is the hard part

Turning audio into a number is only half the job. The score also has to mean something close to what a teacher would say. In the feasibility test, ten learners were scored by both an Ustaz and the app. The two sets of scores moved together with a correlation of 0.51, and the app generally landed higher than the human judge.
A moderate correlation means the score is a practice guide, not a final assessment.
A consistent upward bias points at the feature weights, which the authors plan to tune.

props.caption: Reading the Quran together, the practice an app supplements. Image: Bisajunisa, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: Where this helps most

The clearest benefit lands with learners who cannot meet a mentor often. A daily score, even an imperfect one, keeps practice moving between sessions. The authors also note that the method still needs more respondents, a fourth acoustic feature based on timbre, and trials at higher Iqro levels before it can be offered as an evaluation tool.
The wider lesson for learning apps is simple. Change the output from a verdict into a measurement, and the learner gains a reason to try again.

Source: Komang Candra Brata, Mohamad Handy Nugraha, and Adam Hendra Brata (2022). An alternative m-learning scoring approach to automatically evaluate Iqro's pronunciation based on pitch, volume, and rhythm features. International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering. DOI:

article.title: Typing With Your Head When Your Hands Are Busy
article.subtitle: A team built a phone keyboard driven entirely by head movement and tested three layouts for it.

content.text: A phone keyboard assumes two free hands. That assumption breaks for a driver, for a welder, and completely for anyone who cannot use their hands at all. A research group at Universitas Brawijaya designed an interface for that situation, where the only input is the movement of the user's head.

props.caption: A simple headset turns a phone into a head tracked screen. Image: Pinguinguy, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: How the input works

The system is called HEMOCS, short for Head Movement Control System. A phone sits inside a dummy head mounted display of the cardboard kind, and its accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer report how the head is oriented. That orientation is described with three angles: pitch, roll, and yaw.
Those angles turn into six gestures. The head can rotate left or right, tilt forward or back, and bend sideways in either direction. Each gesture can be bound to an action on screen.

props.caption: Headset interfaces are awkward to test without help. Image: Subhashish Panigrahi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Three layouts, two control styles

The prototype keyboard was built three times over, with letters arranged by English frequency, in plain alphabetical order, and in the familiar QWERTY order. Two control styles were tried as well. In free movement the head drives a pointer like a mouse, and a key is selected by holding still for three seconds. In linear movement, gestures step the pointer around and fire actions directly.
Frequency layout: 99 head movements on average
Alphabetical layout: 106 movements
QWERTY layout: 119 movements

Other settings were tuned by experiment. A head angle threshold of 12 degrees gave the highest accuracy, at 87 percent, and the best key size came out at 0.3 cm. A small usability session with five respondents followed the measurements.

props.caption: Head control is hands free, but it is not effortless. Image: Skydeas, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The closing result is a tradeoff the authors report plainly. The frequency layout saved the most movement, yet users still felt more comfortable with QWERTY because it was familiar, while the frequency arrangement was judged easier to use. Linear movement was preferred over free movement, and respondents mentioned some mental and physical strain. The authors note their layouts and controls can help builders pick the right combination for hands free interaction, with the next step being a real HEMOCS application.

Source: Herman Tolle et al. (2016). Design of keyboard input control for mobile application using Head Movement Control (HEMOCS). 2016 International Conference on Advanced Computer Science and Information Systems (ICACSIS). DOI:

article.title: The Hidden Cost of a Good Concept Map Lesson
article.subtitle: Teachers spend hours building the map their students will rebuild. A study tested whether software can carry part of that load.

content.text: A teaching method only survives if teachers can afford the time it takes. That is the quiet problem behind many good classroom ideas, and it is the problem this research set out to solve.

In Kit-Build concept mapping, students recompose the teacher's map from its parts. The activity depends entirely on one artefact that a teacher has to produce first. Building it by hand takes hours, and the effort repeats for every passage.
Where the effort goes

The authors separate the work into two jobs. One is reading and deciding which ideas matter. The other is typing those decisions in as nodes and labelled links. The second job is mechanical, and it is the one a machine can help with.

props.caption: Kit-Build works like this: split the map into parts, then let students rebuild it. Credit: Patafisik, CC BY-SA 3.0.

content.text: Their support tool reads the passage and offers keywords and relationship phrases as candidates. The teacher accepts, edits or ignores them. The design bet is that reviewing suggestions is faster than writing from a blank canvas.
Three practical lessons
Keep the human in the loop. The tool suggests, the teacher decides. Fully automatic generation was rejected because a good map reflects a judgement about what a class needs.
Familiarise people first. Participants got a practice task two weeks before the trial, so the tool itself was not the thing being learned during measurement.
Check quality, not just speed. Bigger maps are worthless if the propositions inside them are wrong, so the study scored map quality alongside map size.

props.caption: The teacher's map decides what the class works with. Credit: Amuzujoe, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: The questionnaire backs up the timing result. Teachers rated the tool as useful on a five-question scale adapted from the Technology Acceptance Model, and the scale showed good internal consistency. Numbers alone rarely convince a teacher to change a routine, but a tool that saves an evening of typing might.
Source: Pinandito et al. (2021). Design and development of semi-automatic concept map authoring support tool. Research and Practice in Technology Enhanced Learning, 16(8). DOI:

article.title: Efficiency and Familiarity Pull in Different Directions
article.subtitle: The head movement keyboard that saved the most effort was not the one users preferred.

content.text: It is easy to optimise for the thing you can count. In an interface driven by head movement, the countable thing is movement itself, so a layout that shaves gestures off a sentence looks like the better layout. A study of head controlled typing shows why that number is not the whole decision.

props.caption: A headset session, observed closely by a helper. Image: Subhashish Panigrahi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The layout that won on paper

Measured purely in motion, the frequency arrangement came first. It took 99 head movements on average, against 106 for alphabetical order and 119 for QWERTY. The gap between the best and the worst is twenty movements, which is a real cost for someone typing with their neck.
What participants said instead

Respondents still preferred QWERTY, and the reason they gave was familiarity rather than comfort. The frequency layout was judged easier to use, so users could feel the difference, but habit weighed more. The same split appeared in the control styles. Linear movement, where gestures step the pointer around, was preferred to free movement, where the head acts as a mouse and a key is chosen by holding still for three seconds.

props.caption: The hardware is a phone inside a cardboard viewer. Image: Evan-Amos, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: What the tuning suggests
Try the unusual layout, but expect the familiar one to win by default
Prefer discrete gestures over free pointing when the input is noisy
Measure strain as well as movement, since participants reported both

That strain note matters for the accessibility case behind this work. Hands free input is often proposed for drivers, for industrial workers, and for people who cannot use a keyboard at all, and for the last group physical effort is not a footnote but a central design constraint. A layout that saves movements while demanding more concentration may be the wrong trade.

The prototype ran on iPhone sensors through CoreMotion, with iOS 7.1 as the floor, and the authors point to a full application as the next step. The lesson to carry forward is that the fastest layout and the preferred layout are two different questions, and a design has to answer both.

Source: Herman Tolle et al. (2016). Design of keyboard input control for mobile application using Head Movement Control (HEMOCS). 2016 International Conference on Advanced Computer Science and Information Systems (ICACSIS). DOI:

article.title: Hanasu: Practising Japanese Out Loud on a Phone
article.subtitle: Most Japanese learning apps drill vocabulary and reading. This one asks the learner to speak and to listen.

content.text: Japanese is one of the most popular foreign languages in Indonesian higher education, and one of the hardest to pick up. The gap between wanting to learn it and being able to hold a conversation is where most self-study efforts stall.

A team at Universitas Brawijaya looked at the apps students already use and found a pattern. Almost all of them train vocabulary, writing and reading. Almost none of them train pronunciation, even though pronunciation is fundamental to the language.
What Hanasu does differently

Hanasu adds listening and speaking exercises to a mobile learning application. A lesson screen pairs an illustration with text and two buttons: an ear for listening practice, a microphone for speaking. The learner hears the phrase, repeats it, and the app treats that spoken input as part of the lesson.

props.caption: The idea is to make the phone the practice partner. Credit: LeanForward lf, CC BY-SA 2.0.

content.text: Text to speech carries the audio side, turning written material into something the learner can hear. That keeps the content pipeline simple: the team writes text, and the device speaks it, rather than recording every phrase by hand.
How it was built and tested

Development started from requirements gathered from students and lecturers, and the interface went through comparison testing to settle on controls that felt natural on a small screen. The application follows a client and server arrangement, with the mobile app on one side and a back end serving content on the other.

props.caption: The classroom version of the same drill. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The evaluation was small and the authors describe the outcomes as preliminary. Their reading is that the listening and speaking approach is feasible for m-learning, and that it showed promising gains against conventional study methods. That is encouragement for a direction, not a finished result.

Source: Komang Candra Brata, Adam Hendra Brata and Eko Prasetyo Lukman (2019). Hanasu: Interactive Japanese language m-learning application to support listening and speaking exercise. Proceedings of the 2019 3rd International Conference on Education and Multimedia Technology (ICEMT 2019), 311-315. DOI:

article.title: Group Travel Decisions Need a Different Ranking Rule
article.subtitle: When several people choose a destination together, plain TOPSIS is no longer enough.

content.text: Tourists rarely travel alone. They bring a friend, a partner, or a family, and the moment more than one person has an opinion, a recommendation gets harder. A study in the Register journal looked at what changes when a mobile decision support system has to rank options for a group rather than for one user.
Ranking for one person

The personal system uses TOPSIS, which ranks options by how close each one sits to the ideal solution. The test case was a place to buy souvenirs in Malang, with fifteen alternatives judged against three criteria.
Distance and price act as cost criteria, so the best value is the smallest one.
How long a shop has been standing acts as a profit criterion, so the best value is the largest one.

props.caption: A group working through a shared choice. Image: eekim, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Ranking for a group

For a group, the team paired TOPSIS with the Borda count. Each decision maker runs their own TOPSIS pass and produces a personal order. Borda then hands the top option the largest number of points and the bottom option the smallest. The group score multiplies each alternative's closeness coefficient by its Borda points and adds the results across users.

props.caption: A street in the Celaket area of Malang. Image: Evan Pasha, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: How well the two agree
The team compared the group recommendation against each member's personal recommendation using correlation testing.
Three of the four users lined up closely with the group result, at 0.97, 0.99, and 0.88.
One user sat further apart at 0.69, and the average across users came to 0.88.

The authors read that as a positive result for group recommendations built on TOPSIS and Borda, while noting the earlier personal system had reached 0.77 on its own. They suggest augmented reality as a direction for future work.

Source: Ratih Kartika Dewi, Eriq Muhammad Adams Jonemaro, Agi Putra Kharisma, Najla Alia Farah, and Mury Fajar Dewantoro (2021). TOPSIS for mobile based group and personal decision support system. Register: Jurnal Ilmiah Teknologi Sistem Informasi. DOI:

article.title: Gim simulasi kehidupan untuk melatih literasi grafik
article.subtitle: Sebuah gim serius dirancang dengan framework DPE, lalu diuji ke 30 responden dengan hasil yang terukur.

content.text: Literasi grafik adalah kemampuan membaca, membandingkan, dan menafsirkan informasi yang disajikan dalam bentuk grafik. Kemampuan ini terdengar sederhana, tetapi hasil survei menunjukkan angkanya rendah. Satu survei terhadap 155 mahasiswa menemukan hanya 43 persen yang memahami tabel dan grafik.

Temuan lain menyebut kurang dari 15 persen siswa kelas delapan mencapai kriteria ketuntasan pada materi grafik. Berangkat dari situ, tiga peneliti Universitas Brawijaya membangun sebuah gim serius bernama Gravic.

props.caption: Seorang siswa mengerjakan latihan di komputer. Literasi grafik jadi target pembelajarannya. Foto: Syced, CC0.

content.text: Gim seperti apa yang dibangun

Gravic adalah gim simulasi kehidupan 2D yang dibuat dengan Unity dan bahasa C#, dengan tampilan bergaya pixel art. Pemain berperan sebagai siswa kelas lima yang belum paham grafik, lalu diajak berkeliling kota oleh gurunya untuk menyelesaikan berbagai misi.
Setiap misi berupa kuis, misalnya menebak nama jenis grafik yang ditampilkan di layar.
NPC di tiap lokasi diberi peran sesuai pekerjaannya, seperti penjual roti bertopi koki.
Jawaban benar mendapat pujian dari NPC, sedangkan jawaban salah masih bisa dicoba lagi.

props.caption: Ilustrasi grafik. Membaca, membandingkan, dan menafsirkan adalah tiga kompetensi intinya. Gambar: LeoBlanchette, CC0.

content.text: Hasil pengujian

Pengujian dibagi dua tahap. Pengujian internal memakai metode black box oleh lima anggota komunitas RAION, dan seluruh kebutuhan fungsional dinyatakan valid. Pengujian eksternal melibatkan 30 responden dengan alur pre-test, bermain, lalu post-test, masing-masing 15 menit.
Rata-rata skor naik dari 70,657 menjadi 81,090 pada skala 100.
Uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk memberi nilai 0,195 dan 0,060, sehingga data dianggap berdistribusi normal.
Uji paired sample t-test menghasilkan signifikansi 0,000, sehingga H0 ditolak.

Artinya ada perbedaan rata-rata yang nyata antara kondisi sebelum dan sesudah bermain. Penulis menyimpulkan bahwa Gravic dapat dipakai sebagai salah satu alternatif media belajar grafik, bukan pengganti pengajaran di kelas.

Sumber: Silitonga, E., Jonemaro, E.M.A., Akbar, M.A. (2023). Pengembangan Gim Simulasi Kehidupan untuk Peningkatan Literasi Grafik Menggunakan Framework DPE. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: Gim Papan Berburu Harta Karun untuk Mengenal Angka
article.subtitle: Sebuah alat permainan edukatif dirancang dengan kerangka MDA dan diuji pada empat siswa taman kanak-kanak.

content.text: Mengenalkan angka kepada anak usia empat sampai lima tahun bukan pekerjaan sederhana. Guru di sebuah taman kanak-kanak dengan fasilitas pembelajaran menengah ke bawah melaporkan kesulitan membawa konsep angka ke dalam kelas. Penelitian di JTIIK merancang solusi berupa alat permainan edukatif, bukan aplikasi.
Bertolak dari alat permainan edukatif

Pendekatan belajar sambil bermain sudah lama dipakai di taman kanak-kanak, dan alat permainannya dikenal sebagai Alat Permainan Edukatif (APE). Masalahnya, tidak semua guru berhasil menerjemahkan alat itu menjadi kegiatan yang sesuai kompetensi kurikulum. Penelitian ini mengisi jeda tersebut dengan merancang APE secara khusus.
Nama gimnya Berburu Harta Karun

Perancangan memakai kerangka MDA, yang membagi gim menjadi tiga komponen: mechanics sebagai aturan, dynamics sebagai jalannya permainan, dan aesthetics sebagai rasa senang yang muncul. Pengembangannya memakai metode iteratif sebanyak delapan kali sampai prototipe dianggap cukup.
Bentuknya permainan papan bernama Berburu Harta Karun, dengan mekanik yang diadaptasi dari ular tangga.
Permainan dimainkan dua siswa dengan satu narator, peran yang diisi guru.
Materinya angka 1 sampai 5 dan 6 sampai 10, mencakup nama, bentuk, dan nilai angka.

props.caption: Halaman bermain sebuah taman kanak-kanak. Foto: Andykatib, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Hasil uji coba terbatas

Penilaian memakai desain One Group Pretest-Posttest terhadap empat siswa, dua di antaranya berada di atas rata-rata kelas dan dua di bawahnya. Setiap anak diminta menyebutkan tiga angka yang diperlihatkan.
Nilai rata-rata pretest 41,67 persen, lalu naik menjadi 75 persen pada posttest.
Uji kesenangan memakai Smileyometer memberi skor 4,48 dari 5, artinya anak-anak sangat senang bermain.

props.caption: Anak-anak bermain di taman kanak-kanak. Foto: State Government Photographer, CC0.

content.text: Peneliti menyimpulkan gim papan ini membantu pemahaman konsep angka pada siswa kelompok A. Mereka juga menyarankan pengujian lanjutan dengan lebih banyak anak pada rentang usia yang sama, karena uji coba ini hanya melibatkan empat siswa di satu sekolah.

Sumber: Abdiel Wahyu Ramadhyono, Eriq Muhammad Adams Jonemaro, dan Tri Afirianto (2024). Perancangan Gim Edukasi Anak Usia Dini untuk Meningkatkan Pemahaman Pengenalan Angka. Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Ilmu Komputer. DOI:

article.title: How a Restaurant App Picks What to Recommend
article.subtitle: Weighting the options, not just the criteria, is where a mobile culinary recommender gets its accuracy.

content.text: Deciding where to eat is a decision with several goals in conflict: nobody wants to walk far, nobody wants to overspend, and everybody wants the food to be good. A 2015 paper in the ARPN Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences tackled that decision for a mobile application, and its contribution sits in an unglamorous place. The useful part is not the criteria. It is how the alternatives are weighted against them.
Where plain AHP runs into trouble

Analytic Hierarchy Process is a familiar way to break a messy choice into a hierarchy of criteria and then compare them in pairs. It works well when the criteria are few. The authors point at the step that follows, where every candidate restaurant has to be scored against every criterion, and argue that this step degrades as the list of alternatives grows. A diner's judgment about one warung against another is rarely crisp, and the comparison matrix starts to misrepresent what the person actually meant.
What the system asks the diner
The mobile application keeps the input short. A user states a budget and a travel radius, and the system filters the candidate list before any weighting happens.
Distance, computed from coordinates with the Haversine formula rather than from a street network.
Price, checked against a stated budget such as Rp 30,000 for a meal.
Rating, the quality signal carried over from the culinary data the system already had.

props.caption: A warung in Pandanwangi, the sort of stall the filters rank. Image: Indonesiagood, CC BY 4.0.

content.text: Fuzzy weights, measured against experts

The modification is to treat the alternative weights as fuzzy rather than exact, which lets a diner express a preference as a range instead of a hard number. The team then ran 30 test cases and compared the application's pick with what human experts chose for the same situations.
The fuzzy alternative weighting matched the expert decision in 66.67 percent of the 30 cases.
The original, non-fuzzy AHP process managed 30 percent on the same cases.

props.caption: Fried rice eaten by hand, a low budget meal the filters surface. Image: Fitrah 913, CC BY 4.0.

content.text: An equal weighting baseline, where every criterion counts the same, matched the experts in about 36.7 percent of cases. That number matters because it sets the floor. Beating a naive average is not much of an achievement. More than doubling it is worth reporting, and it suggests the vague, human way of comparing two restaurants carries real information that a crisp matrix throws away.
Source: Pinandito et al. (2015). Alternatives Weighting in Analytic Hierarchy Process of Mobile Culinary Recommendation System Using Fuzzy. ARPN Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences.

article.title: What Students Thought of the Extended Scratch-Build Map Tool
article.subtitle: The method already improved comprehension. This study asked whether learners wanted to keep using it.

content.text: A tool can improve test scores and still be abandoned. Students may find it confusing, slow, or simply not worth the effort, and by the next semester nobody opens it. Acceptance research exists to measure that gap.

A study from Hiroshima University, Universitas Negeri Malang and Universitas Brawijaya looked at Extended Scratch-Build, a computer based tool for extending concept maps. Earlier work had shown the approach improves understanding and knowledge structure. What was missing was evidence about whether learners wanted to keep using it.
How the tool works

Extended Scratch-Build is an open-ended extension tool. A student starts from a concept map they already built, then expands it with new concepts, links and examples as their understanding grows. Nothing is prescribed, so the map stays personal.

props.caption: Concept mapping software in use. Credit: Madhav kiran sodum, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: How the team asked

The team used the Technology Acceptance Model, a long standing framework for questions like this. Three constructs carried the survey: perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and behavioral intention, which is the student's stated plan to keep using the tool.

props.caption: Where a tool like this gets tested. Credit: Narek75, CC BY-SA 4.0.

content.text: What the team found

Students responded positively on all three constructs. They found the tool easy to use and described it as a valuable learning tool. They also agreed that the approach is promising and suitable for future learning.

That is a modest but useful result. Acceptance is not the same thing as learning, and the authors present it as one piece of the picture rather than proof of anything. Still, a tool students intend to keep using is a tool with a chance to change how they study.

Source: Prasetya et al. (2021). Analysis of Perceived Ease of Use, Perceived Usefulness, and Behavioral Intention on Extended Scratch-Build Concept Mapping Tool. 2021 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Information Engineering (ICEEIE), 1-5. DOI:

article.title: Extended Kit Build: Steady Progress Instead of a Late Slide
article.subtitle: Pairing a closed mapping task with an open one, and what that does to the back half of a course.

content.text: Two phase mapping looks like a small twist on a familiar exercise. Students build a map, then extend it as new material arrives. The order turns out to matter more than it sounds, because the first phase decides how the second one goes.

props.caption: Topics branching out from one subject. Image: Supriyabah, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: In the Kit Build version, phase one is a reconstruction. The teacher's map is broken into loose concepts and links, and students assemble them again. Nothing is mysterious about what a good map looks like, because the pieces themselves carry the structure.
Closed first, open second

Phase two switches to open mapping. Students add their own concepts, links, and propositions for the next subtopic. That pairing is the whole idea. Closed work builds a reliable base, and open work tests whether students can carry it somewhere new.
Phase one gives everyone the same starting structure.
Phase two lets individual understanding show through.

props.caption: Ideas arranged around one centre point. Image: Tanjatod, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: What held steady

Across 55 students, the group that began with the kit scored higher on knowledge structure quality, and their scores were spread more evenly across the subtopics. The first two subtopics showed little difference. The third produced the largest gap in the study.

Consistency is the part worth noticing. The kit group held its performance from the start of the material to the end, which suggests the approach keeps students from losing their footing as topics get harder.

That matters in a course with a sequence to get through. A method that helps strongly at subtopic three, and only slightly at subtopic one, is doing its work exactly where students usually start to drift.
The practical lesson is to treat the phases as separate tools. Use reconstruction to align everyone on the basics, then open the map up and let students build something of their own on top of it.

Source: Prasetya et al. (2021). Investigating the Distribution of Knowledge Structure in Extended Concept Mapping. Proceedings of the Business Innovation and Engineering Conference 2020, Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research. DOI:

article.title: Which Concept Mapping Style Helps Students Remember More?
article.subtitle: A two-week delayed test separated two ways of extending a concept map.

content.text: Concept maps come in more than one flavour, and the differences are not cosmetic. Some ask students to build freely from a blank canvas. Others hand them a fixed set of pieces and ask them to reassemble what the teacher had in mind. A study from Indonesia put two of these designs side by side, then waited two weeks to see what stuck.

props.caption: A concept map built by hand. Image: Chabre, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Both designs work in two phases. Phase one produces a map of the core material. Phase two extends that map with a second round of content. Where they differ is what students get during phase one.
Two ways to extend a map

Extended Scratch-Build is open ended. Students choose their own concepts and links. Extended Kit-Build starts closed: students recompose a map from pieces taken out of the teacher's map, then extend it freely in phase two.
Open ended: learners decide every concept and link themselves.
Closed then extended: learners rebuild the teacher's map first, then add their own pieces.

props.caption: A university class working through a mapping exercise. Image: Harrison Keely, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Fifty-five second-year students in a Database course took part, split into a control group of 27 and an experimental group of 28. Both sat an immediate test after the activity and a delayed test 14 days later, using the same questions in a different order.
What the delayed test showed

The kit-build group scored higher on the immediate test, 87.50 against 81.02, and stayed ahead after two weeks, 78.57 against 69.91. Both groups lost ground over the fortnight. The gap between them held.

The clearest difference appeared on questions tied to the kit itself. Questions covering material outside the kit showed no significant gap. In other words, the advantage tracks the parts of the map students had to piece together rather than simply read.

props.caption: The course covered relational databases. Image: RRZEicons, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Source: Prasetya et al. (2022). Investigating the memory retention in extension concept mapping. Improving Assessment and Evaluation Strategies on Online Learning. DOI:

article.title: Enam Fungsi Dasar Sebuah Dasbor Learning Analytics
article.subtitle: Rancangan dasbor untuk personalized learning berangkat dari kebutuhan pengguna, lalu diterjemahkan menjadi daftar fungsi yang harus ada.

content.text: Gaya belajar mahasiswa berbeda beda, tetapi banyak sistem pembelajaran daring memberi perlakuan yang sama kepada semua orang. Materi dan urutan belajar yang cocok untuk satu mahasiswa bisa terasa salah untuk mahasiswa lain.
Penelitian ini membahas langkah sebelum aplikasi dibangun, yaitu merancang solusi dasbor Learning Analytics yang dapat menjadi masukan bagi model personalized learning.
Pendekatan yang dipakai

Tim peneliti memakai Human-centered Design. Kebutuhan pengguna digali lebih dulu, lalu diterjemahkan menjadi daftar kebutuhan sistem. Cara ini membuat rancangan bertumpu pada pengalaman mahasiswa, bukan pada asumsi pengembang.
Hasilnya dibagi dua kelompok. Kebutuhan fungsional menjelaskan apa yang harus bisa dilakukan sistem. Kebutuhan non fungsional menjelaskan seberapa baik sistem harus melakukannya.

props.caption: Mahasiswa mengerjakan tugas dengan laptop. Foto: Kwameghana, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Enam fungsi yang dihasilkan
Rancangan dasbor menghasilkan enam kebutuhan fungsional: fungsi login, akses daftar materi, membuka detail materi, evaluasi materi, rangkuman aktivitas, dan logout.

Daftar itu sederhana, dan justru itu yang membuatnya berguna. Setiap fungsi adalah titik pengumpulan data. Dari aktivitas membuka materi dan mengerjakan evaluasi, dasbor dapat membaca pola belajar seorang mahasiswa. Pola itulah yang nanti dipakai untuk menyesuaikan materi dengan gaya belajarnya.

props.caption: Seorang mahasiswa membaca dari layar laptop. Foto: Jaokov, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Perlu dicatat bahwa penelitian ini berhenti pada tahap rancangan. Yang dihasilkan adalah kebutuhan sistem sebagai dasar pengumpulan data, bukan aplikasi yang sudah diuji ke mahasiswa. Posisi itu penting supaya harapan tidak melebihi bukti.
Bagi tim yang ingin membangun dasbor serupa, urutan kerja ini layak ditiru: sepakati lebih dulu data apa yang ingin dibaca, lalu tentukan fitur apa yang harus ada untuk menghasilkannya.
Sumber: Wardhono, Kharisma, dan Jonemaro (2022). Pengembangan Desain Solusi Dasbor Learning Analytics sebagai Input pada Model Personalized Learning. Edunity: Kajian Ilmu Sosial dan Pendidikan. DOI:

article.title: Eleven Factors That Shape Productivity in Work From Anywhere
article.subtitle: A systematic review pulls scattered research into one list of what actually moves the needle.

content.text: Work From Anywhere has stopped being an emergency arrangement. Many companies now run office days and remote days side by side, and they want to know whether the mix works. That question needs evidence, and the evidence has been scattered across dozens of separate studies.

props.caption: Remote work from a laptop. Image: perzon seo, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The authors used a Systematic Literature Review, the same approach medical researchers use to summarise a field. They fixed their search criteria before they started: keywords, publication years and journal quality. Then they screened candidates on topic and language, on abstract, and finally on full content.
Adding a reliability check

Screening literature is usually a judgement call, and judgement drifts. To reduce that bias the team screened each paper twice and measured agreement between rounds using Cohen's Kappa. It makes a subjective process measurably more objective, and shows a reader how much trust to place in the selection.

props.caption: Working away from the office. Image: CruiseAmerica, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Seventeen studies survived the full screening. From them the authors extracted eleven factors that influence employee productivity when work is not tied to a building.
Environment and adequate technology cover the physical setup: where a person works and whether the tools hold up.
Time efficiency, cost efficiency and geographical flexibility describe what the arrangement buys: hours saved on commuting and freedom to choose a location.
Psychology, health and employee personality point inward. Mood, physical wellbeing and individual temperament all change how much someone gets done at home.
Salary, gender and communication are the organisational factors. Pay shapes motivation, and communication quality decides whether a distributed team stays coordinated.

The list is broad on purpose, and that is the most useful thing about it. Productivity in a distributed setting is not one variable to optimise. It is a bundle of working conditions, personal circumstances and management practices that move together.
The authors frame the result as groundwork. Their goal is to model the business processes a company needs to evaluate and improve a Work From Anywhere system, and a needs analysis comes first.
Source: Fauziyah et al. (2024). Factors Influencing Employee Productivity in Work From Anywhere: A Systematic Literature Review (SLR). Journal of Information Technology and Computer Science. DOI:

article.title: Why Learning Tools Get Abandoned After the Study Ends
article.subtitle: A concept mapping trial measured something most evaluations skip: whether students wanted to keep the tool.

content.text: A common way to evaluate a learning tool is to measure outcomes. Did the group using it score higher than the group that did not? That question is worth asking, and also only half the picture.
The other half is use. A tool that raises scores inside a supervised trial can still die the moment the trial ends, because the people who would use it find it awkward or do not see the point.
What this study measured instead

A team from Hiroshima University, Universitas Negeri Malang and Universitas Brawijaya ran a perception study on Extended Scratch-Build, a tool that lets learners extend a concept map they have already built. Instead of testing whether it improved understanding, they asked how students felt about it.

props.caption: Students sketching ideas by hand, the low tech version of the same task. Image: CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: They used the Technology Acceptance Model, a framework from information systems research that has been borrowed widely by education researchers for exactly this purpose. Three constructs do the work: perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and behavioral intention.
What the team learned

Students gave positive responses on all three. They described the tool as easy to use and as valuable for learning, and they agreed it was promising for future learning. The team reads that as support for continuing to develop the approach.

props.caption: Classroom devices only help if students choose to return to them. Credit: Aigner Ronja and Kohlmeier Michelle, CC0.

content.text: There is a caution attached to that reading. Perception data is self report, gathered in the moment, from students who had just finished using the tool. It predicts intention, not behaviour, and the two do not always agree over a semester.
What to take from it
Measure acceptance alongside outcomes. Scores tell you whether a tool worked once. Acceptance tells you whether it has a future.
Ease of use is a design variable, not a fixed property of the software. Clarity in the interface shows up directly in whether people keep going.
Positive perception is a green light for further work, not a finish line. The authors leave the harder questions open.

Source: Prasetya et al. (2021). Analysis of Perceived Ease of Use, Perceived Usefulness, and Behavioral Intention on Extended Scratch-Build Concept Mapping Tool. 2021 7th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Information Engineering (ICEEIE), 1-5. DOI:

article.title: Making Dijkstra Faster by Throwing Away Points
article.subtitle: A line simplification step before the search cuts memory use and computation time on resource limited phones.

content.text: Open a map app and ask for directions. Behind that tap, an algorithm walks through a graph of roads to find the shortest path. Most of the time it feels instant, but on a cheap phone with a dense route network it can crawl.

The Dijkstra algorithm is the workhorse of routing, and its cost scales with the data it receives. Every extra point on a route line is another node to examine. A bus line that curves through a city can carry hundreds of points that describe the shape of the road rather than a real decision point.
The idea behind the fix

The team applied the Douglas-Peucker algorithm as a cleaning step before routing. The method walks along a line and removes points that sit close to the straight segment between their neighbours. What remains is a simpler line with the same overall shape. Feed that simpler graph into Dijkstra and there is far less to compute.

props.caption: A graph structure of the kind routing algorithms traverse. Image: Logan Essex, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: To test the idea, the researchers used public transport routes in Malang City, Indonesia. They measured how long the algorithm took and how much memory it used on an Android device, repeating each measurement many times so that a single slow run could not distort the result.
What the team found
Running line simplification before Dijkstra reduced both the time needed to compute a route and the memory the process consumed.
The gain came from the data preparation step, not from a rewrite of the search algorithm itself.

props.caption: A street in Malang City, the study area. Photo: sugeng widodo, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The result matters because the same trade-off shows up everywhere. Routing libraries are tuned for servers with plenty of headroom, while phones have far less. Anything that shrinks the input before the search begins buys performance without touching the parts of the system that already work.

props.caption: Public transport on a Malang street. Photo: Mujiono Ma'ruf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: For anyone building transit or delivery apps, the lesson is cheap to apply. Simplify the line geometry before you search it. The picture on screen stays the same, and the device has less work to do on every single request.

Source: Muhammad Yasir Anshari Haq, Riswan Septriayadi Sianturi, and Aryo Pinandito (2023). Enhancing the Efficiency of Navigation Systems: Dijkstra Algorithm Optimization Through Integration of Douglas-Peucker Line Simplification Technique. Proceedings of the 8th International Conference on Sustainable Information Engineering and Technology. DOI:

article.title: Cutting the Points That Slow Down a Route Finder
article.subtitle: Simplifying route geometry before the search can cut processing time by four fifths.

content.text: Public transport apps promise to find you a route in seconds. Under the hood, many of them run Dijkstra's algorithm, which walks through a network of stops and connections looking for the shortest way from A to B. It is reliable and well understood. It is also slow once the network gets big, because it keeps looking at every option it can reach.

props.caption: A weighted graph of the kind Dijkstra's algorithm searches. Image: Bensterbenk, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: A team at Universitas Brawijaya asked a different question. What if the network were smaller before the search even began? Their answer was to run the Douglas-Peucker line simplification algorithm over the route geometry first, thinning out the points that add detail without adding meaning.
Two algorithms, one pipeline

Douglas-Peucker takes a line and drops points that sit very close to the straight line between their neighbours. What survives is a coarser shape that still follows the original path. Fewer points means fewer nodes for Dijkstra to work through.
The simplification step costs a little on its own: 0.5% extra memory and 5.13% extra processing time.
In exchange, the overall memory footprint fell by 72.56%.
Overall processing time fell by 80.83%.

props.caption: Dijkstra's algorithm expanding outward from a start node. Image: Ibmua, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: The paper also checks that the drawn route still looks right. Aggressive simplification can turn a curving road into a straight line that cuts across buildings, so the authors tuned the process to keep the displayed path reasonably consistent with the real one. The visual cue survives, which matters because a route line that ignores the road is worse than a slow one.
Why it matters

Route finding is a feature users notice only when it is slow. Shaving four fifths off the processing time is the difference between a map that responds while you type and one that makes you wait. The overhead is paid once per simplify operation, while the savings apply to every search that follows.

props.caption: Angkot on a Malang street. Image: Annidafattiya, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

content.text: Source: Pinandito, Kharisma, and Akbar (2023). Improving Route-Finding Performance of Dijkstra Algorithm and Maintaining Path Visual Cue Using Douglas-Peucker Algorithm. Proceedings of the 8th International Conference on Sustainable Information Engineering and Technology. DOI:

article.title: Digital Maps Win on Speed, AR Wins on Feeling
article.subtitle: A field study in Taiwan put two pedestrian navigation interfaces head to head and found the tradeoff is not about accuracy.

content.text: Pedestrian navigation apps mostly show you the same thing: a flat map with a blue dot and a route line. Location based augmented reality offers an alternative, overlaying directions on the camera view of the street ahead. Which one actually helps you walk to your destination faster?

A field study in Taiwan put the question to the test. The authors built two versions of the same bus stop finder, one using a 2D map interface and one using location based AR, and gave both to the same ten participants.
How the comparison worked

Participants were students aged 20 to 28 who used Android phones daily and did not know the test area. The study ran in Zhongli District, Taoyuan City. Each person completed two scenarios: a blind search, where they had to find a location given only as a name, and a directed search, where they picked a nearby place and followed the guidance.
